title.zh: 卷一百六十八 列傳第五十五: 陳祐 劉宣 何榮祖 陳思濟 秦長卿 趙與□ 姚天福 許國禎
title.en: Volume 168 Biographies 55: Chen You, Liu Xuan, He Rongzu, Chen Siji, Qin Zhangqing, Zhao Yu□, Yao Tianfu, Xu Guozhen
title.raw: 卷一百六十八 列傳第五十五: 陳祐 劉宣 何榮祖 陳思濟 秦長卿 趙與□ 姚天福 許國禎 Volume 168 Biographies 55: Chen You, Liu Xuan, He Rongzu, Chen Siji, Qin Zhangqing, Zhao Yu□, Yao Tianfu, Xu Guozhen

sentences.zh: 陳祐 天祥

translations.literal: Chen You; Tianxiang
translations.idiomatic: Chen You and Tianxiang

sentences.zh: 陳祐，一名天祐，字慶甫，趙州寧晉人，世業農。

translations.literal: Chen You, one name Tianyou, styled Qingfu, a man of Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture; his family farmed for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Chen You, also known as Tianyou and styled Qingfu, was a native of Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture; his family had farmed for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖忠，博究經史，鄉黨皆尊而師之，既歿，門人諡曰茂行先生。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhong thoroughly investigated the classics and histories; the village all honored and took him as teacher. After his death, disciples gave the posthumous title Master of Abundant Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhong had mastered the classics and histories; everyone in the village honored and looked to him as a teacher. After his death, his disciples gave him the posthumous title Master of Abundant Conduct.

sentences.zh: 祐少好學，家貧，母張氏嘗剪髮易書使讀之，長遂博通經史。

translations.literal: You from youth loved learning. The family was poor; his mother Lady Zhang once cut her hair to exchange for books for him to read. When grown, he then broadly mastered the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: You loved learning from an early age. The family was poor, and his mother, Lady Zhang, once cut her hair to trade for books so he could read. When he grew up, he attained a broad mastery of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 時諸王得自辟官屬，歲癸丑，穆王府署祐為其府尚書，賜其父母銀十鋌、錦衣一襲。

translations.literal: At the time the princes could themselves recruit staff. In the year guichou, the Prince of Mu's establishment appointed You as Director of his princely household and bestowed on his parents ten ingots of silver and one suit of brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the princes were permitted to recruit their own staff. In the guichou year, the Prince of Mu appointed You as Director of his princely household and gave his parents ten ingots of silver and a suit of brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 王既分土於陝、洛，表祐為河南府總管。

translations.literal: After the prince was granted territory in Shaanxi and Luoyang, he memorialized the court to appoint You Chief Administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince was granted territory in Shaanxi and Luoyang, he recommended You for appointment as Chief Administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 下車之日，首禮金季名士李國維、楊杲、李微、薛玄，諮訪治道，商議古今，奏免征西軍數百家及椒竹諸稅、糧料等錢，又上便民二十餘事，朝廷皆從之。

translations.literal: On the day he took office, he first paid respects to the Jin-dynasty scholars Li Guowei, Yang Gao, Li Wei, and Xue Xuan, consulting on methods of governance and discussing past and present. He memorialized exemption for several hundred households of the Western Army and taxes on pepper, bamboo, grain provisions, and the like, and submitted more than twenty measures to benefit the people; the court approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took office, he first paid his respects to the eminent Jin-dynasty scholars Li Guowei, Yang Gao, Li Wei, and Xue Xuan, consulting them on governance and debating matters past and present. He memorialized tax exemptions for several hundred households of the Western Army and for levies on pepper, bamboo, grain provisions, and the like, and submitted more than twenty proposals to benefit the people; the court approved them all.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，分陝、洛為河南西路。

translations.literal: When Kublai ascended the throne, Shaanxi and Luoyang were divided to form the Henan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai came to the throne, Shaanxi and Luoyang were separated out as the Henan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，真除祐為總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, You was formally appointed Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhongtong reign, You received a formal appointment as Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 時州縣官以未給俸，多貪暴，祐獨以清慎見稱，在官八年，如始至之日。

translations.literal: At the time district and county officials, receiving no salaries, were mostly greedy and violent; You alone was praised for integrity and caution. During eight years in office, he was as on the day he first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: At that time district and county officials, receiving no salaries, were mostly greedy and abusive; You alone was known for integrity and discretion. Through eight years in office he remained as upright as on the day he arrived.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，調官法行，改南京路治中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, when the official transfer law took effect, he was changed to Assistant Administrator of Nanjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhiyuan reign, when the official rotation law took effect, he was reassigned as Assistant Administrator of Nanjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 適東方大蝗，徐、邳尤甚，責捕至急。

translations.literal: Just then there was a great locust plague in the east, especially severe in Xu and Pi; the demand for locust-catching was extremely urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a great locust plague struck the east, worst of all in Xu and Pi, and the pressure to catch locusts was intense.

sentences.zh: 祐部民丁數万人至其地，謂左右曰：「捕蝗慮其傷稼也，今蝗雖盛，而谷已熟，不如令早刈之，庶力小而有得。

translations.literal: You led tens of thousands of laborers from his district to that place and said to those around him: "Catching locusts is because one fears they will harm the crops. Now although the locusts are abundant, the grain is already ripe; better to have them harvest early—perhaps with little effort some gain can still be made."
translations.idiomatic: You took tens of thousands of laborers from his district to the affected area and said to those around him: "We catch locusts because we fear they will ruin the crops. The locusts may be thick now, but the grain is already ripe; it would be better to have people harvest early, so that even a small effort might still yield something."

sentences.zh: 」或以事涉專擅，不可，祐曰：「救民獲罪，亦所甘心。

translations.literal: " Some said the matter involved acting on one's own authority and could not be done. You said: "To save the people and receive punishment—I would gladly accept that."
translations.idiomatic: Some objected that this would amount to unauthorized action and could not be done. You replied: "If saving the people means punishment for me, I would accept that gladly."

sentences.zh: 」即諭之使散去，兩州之民皆賴焉。

translations.literal: " He immediately instructed them to disperse; the people of both prefectures all relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them to disperse, and the people of both prefectures were saved by his decision.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝廷以祐降官無名，乃賜虎符，授嘉議大夫、衛輝路總管​​。

translations.literal: In the third year, the court, seeing that You's demotion had no justification, then bestowed a tiger tally and appointed him Jiayi Doctor and Chief Administrator of Weihui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, seeing that You's demotion had been unjustified, the court granted him a tiger tally and appointed him Jiayi Doctor and Chief Administrator of Weihui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 衛當四方之衝，號為難治，祐申明法令，創立孔子廟，修比干墓，且請於朝著於祀典。

translations.literal: Weihui stood at the crossroads of four directions and was called difficult to govern. You made clear the laws and regulations, established a temple to Confucius, restored the tomb of Bi Gan, and memorialized the court to include them in the state cult.
translations.idiomatic: Weihui lay at a crossroads of four directions and had a reputation for being hard to govern. You clarified the laws and regulations, founded a temple to Confucius, restored the tomb of Bi Gan, and petitioned the court to include both in the official sacrificial canon.

sentences.zh: 及去官，民為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: When he left office, the people erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, the people erected a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 嘗上書世祖，言樹太平之本有三：一曰太子國本，建立宜早；

translations.literal: He once memorialized Kublai, saying that to establish the foundation of great peace there were three things: first, the crown prince is the foundation of the state—the establishment should be early;
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to Kublai, saying that to lay the foundations of lasting peace there were three essentials: first, the crown prince is the root of the state, and his establishment should come early;

sentences.zh: 二曰中書政本，責成宜專；

translations.literal: second, the Secretariat is the foundation of government—accountability should be concentrated;
translations.idiomatic: second, the Secretariat is the root of government, and responsibility for it should be concentrated;

sentences.zh: 三曰人材治本，選舉宜審。

translations.literal: third, talent is the foundation of governance—selection and appointment should be careful.
translations.idiomatic: third, talent is the root of good governance, and selection and appointment should be rigorous.

sentences.zh: 事雖未能盡行，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Although the matters could not all be fully carried out, contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Not all of his proposals could be fully implemented, but contemporary opinion praised them.

sentences.zh: 六年，置提刑按察司，首以祐為山東東西道提刑按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Commission for the Investigation of Crimes was established; You was the first appointed Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Shandong East and West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the Commission for the Investigation of Crimes was established, You became its first Commissioner for the Shandong East and West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時中書、尚書二省並立，世祖厭其煩，欲合為一，集大臣雜議之，祐還朝，特命預其議。

translations.literal: At the time the Secretariat and the Ministry stood side by side; Kublai found this burdensome and wished to merge them into one. He gathered the ministers for joint discussion. You had returned to court and was specially ordered to participate in the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Secretariat and the Ministry existed side by side; Kublai found the arrangement cumbersome and wished to merge them into one. He convened the senior ministers for discussion, and You, having returned to court, was specially ordered to take part.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬為尚書平章政事，欲奏升中書右丞相安童為太師，因罷中書省，懼祐有異議，許進祐為尚書參知政事以噉之。

translations.literal: Ahmad was Vice Director of the Ministry; he wished to memorialize promoting Right Director of the Secretariat An Tong to Grand Preceptor and thereby abolishing the Secretariat. Fearing You would dissent, he promised to promote You to Vice Director of the Ministry to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad, Vice Director of the Ministry, planned to memorialize promoting An Tong, the Right Director of the Secretariat, to Grand Preceptor and thereby abolishing the Secretariat. Fearing You would object, he promised to advance You to Vice Director of the Ministry to win him over.

sentences.zh: 及入議，祐極言中書政本，祖宗所立，不可罷；

translations.literal: When entering the discussion, You strongly argued that the Secretariat was the foundation of government, established by the ancestors, and could not be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: When the discussion began, You argued forcefully that the Secretariat was the foundation of government, established by the founding emperors, and could not be abolished;

sentences.zh: 三公古官，今徒存其虛位，未須設。

translations.literal: the Three Dukes were ancient offices that now existed only in name—there was no need to establish them.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Dukes were ancient offices that now existed only as empty titles, and there was no need to establish them.

sentences.zh: 事遂罷。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬怒其忤己，除祐僉中興等路行尚書省事。

translations.literal: Ahmad, angry that he had defied him, assigned You as Commissioner of the Ministry for the Zhongxing and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad, furious at being crossed, reassigned You as Commissioner of the Branch Ministry for the Zhongxing and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 西涼隸永昌王府，其達魯花赤及總管為人誣構，家各百餘口，王欲悉致之法，祐力辨其冤。

translations.literal: Xiliang was subordinate to the Prince of Yongchang's establishment. Its darughachi and chief administrator were falsely accused by others; each family had over a hundred members. The prince wished to have them all brought to trial. You vigorously argued for their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang fell under the Prince of Yongchang's jurisdiction. Its darughachi and chief administrator had been falsely accused; more than a hundred people in each household were implicated. The prince wanted them all prosecuted, but You forcefully argued their innocence.

sentences.zh: 王怒甚，祐執議彌固，王亦尋悟，二人皆獲免，持祐泣曰：「公再生父母也。」

translations.literal: The prince was very angry; You held to his view all the more firmly. The prince soon came to understand; both men were spared. They held You and wept, saying: "Sir, you are our second parents."
translations.idiomatic: The prince was furious, but You held all the more firmly to his position. The prince soon saw reason, and both men were spared. They clasped You and wept, saying, "You are our second parents."

sentences.zh: 朝廷大舉伐宋，遣祐簽軍，山東民多逃匿，聞祐來，皆曰：「陳按察來，必無私。

translations.literal: The court launched a major campaign against Song and dispatched You to conscript troops. The people of Shandong had mostly fled and hidden themselves. When they heard You was coming, they all said: "Intendant Chen is coming; he will certainly be fair."
translations.idiomatic: The court launched a major campaign against the Song and dispatched You to conscript troops. Many people in Shandong had fled and gone into hiding, but when they heard You was coming, they all said, "Intendant Chen is on his way; he will surely be fair."

sentences.zh: 」遂皆出，應期而辦。

translations.literal: " They all then came out and fulfilled their obligations on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: They all came forward and fulfilled their obligations on schedule.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授南京總管，兼開封府尹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was appointed Chief Administrator of Nanjing and concurrently Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, he was appointed Chief Administrator of Nanjing and concurrently Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 吏多震懾失措，祐因謂曰：「何必若是！

translations.literal: The clerks were mostly shaken and at a loss. You therefore said to them: "Why must it be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: Many of the clerks were frightened and at a loss. You therefore said to them, "Why behave like this!"

sentences.zh: 前為盜跖，今為顏子，吾以顏子待之；

translations.literal: If before you were robbers and now you are like Yan Hui, I will treat you as Yan Hui;
translations.idiomatic: If you were robbers before and are like Yan Hui now, I will treat you as Yan Hui;

sentences.zh: 前為顏子，今為盜跖，吾以盜跖待之。

translations.literal: if before you were like Yan Hui and now you are robbers, I will treat you as robbers."
translations.idiomatic: if you were like Yan Hui before and are robbers now, I will treat you as robbers."

sentences.zh: 」由是吏知修飭，不敢弄法。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the clerks knew to behave themselves and did not dare manipulate the law.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the clerks knew to conduct themselves properly and did not dare manipulate the law.

sentences.zh: 許、蔡間有巨盜，聚眾劫掠，祐捕之急，逃入宋境；

translations.literal: Between Xu and Cai there was a great bandit who gathered followers to plunder. You pressed the pursuit hard; he fled into Song territory;
translations.idiomatic: Between Xu and Cai there was a notorious bandit who gathered followers to plunder. You pressed the pursuit hard, and the man fled into Song territory;

sentences.zh: 宋亡，隨制置夏貴過汴，祐斥下馬，撾殺之於市，民間帖然。

translations.literal: When Song fell, he followed Prefect Xia Gui past Bian. You ordered him pulled from his horse and beaten to death in the marketplace; the people were completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fell, he followed the prefect Xia Gui through Bian. You had him pulled from his horse and beaten to death in the marketplace, and the people were thoroughly pacified.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷浙東道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時江南初附，軍士俘虜溫、台民男女數千口，祐悉奪還之。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangnan had just been incorporated; soldiers had captured several thousand men and women from Wen and Tai prefectures as prisoners. You reclaimed and returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan had only recently submitted, and soldiers had taken several thousand men and women from Wen and Tai prefectures as captives. You reclaimed them all and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行省榷民商酒稅，祐請曰：「兵火之餘，傷殘之民，宜從寬卹。

translations.literal: Before long, the Branch Secretariat imposed wine taxes on merchants. You petitioned: "After the fires of war, the battered populace should receive lenient relief."
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the Branch Secretariat imposed wine taxes on merchants. You petitioned, "After the devastation of war, the battered populace should be treated with leniency."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He received no reply.

sentences.zh: 遣祐檢覆慶元、台州民田。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to inspect the civilian fields of Qingyuan and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to inspect the civilian fields of Qingyuan and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 及還至新昌，值玉山鄉盜，倉猝不及為備，遂遇害，年五十六。

translations.literal: On his return he reached Xinchang and encountered bandits from Yushan township. Caught unprepared, he was killed. He was fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reached Xinchang and ran into bandits from Yushan township. Taken by surprise and unable to defend himself, he was killed. He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 詔贈推忠秉義全節功臣、江浙等處行中書省左丞，追封河南郡公，諡忠定。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously conferred on him the title Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Righteousness, and Preserved Integrity in Full, Left Director of the Branch Secretariat of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and ennobled him as Duke of Henan Commandery with the posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously conferred on him the title Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Righteousness, and Preserved Integrity in Full, appointed him Left Director of the Branch Secretariat of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, ennobled him as Duke of Henan Commandery, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongding.

sentences.zh: 父老請留葬會稽，不得，乃立祠祀之。

translations.literal: The elders requested to bury him in Kuaiji but were not permitted; they therefore erected a shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The local elders asked that he be buried in Kuaiji, but permission was denied; they erected a shrine to honor him instead.

sentences.zh: 祐能詩文，有《節齊集》。

translations.literal: You could write poetry and prose; he had a collection called Jiezhai ji.
translations.idiomatic: You was accomplished in poetry and prose and left a collection entitled Jiezhai ji.

sentences.zh: 子夔，芍陂屯田萬戶，初在揚州，聞祐遇盜死，泣請於行省，願复父讎，擒其賊魁，戮於紹興市。

translations.literal: His son Kui was Commander of the Shaobo Colonization Agricultural Households. Originally stationed at Yangzhou, when he heard his father had been killed by bandits, he wept and petitioned the Branch Secretariat, requesting to avenge his father. He captured the ringleader and executed him in the marketplace of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kui was Commander of the Shaobo Colonization Agricultural Households. Stationed at Yangzhou, when he learned his father had been killed by bandits, he wept and petitioned the Branch Secretariat to avenge him. He captured the ringleader and executed him in the marketplace of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 皋，昌國州知州。

translations.literal: Gao was Prefect of Changguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao served as Prefect of Changguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奭，侍儀司通事舍人。

translations.literal: Shi was Usher of the Ceremonial Service Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served as Usher of the Ceremonial Service Bureau.

sentences.zh: 孫思魯，襲芍陂屯田萬戶。

translations.literal: His grandson Silu inherited the position of Commander of the Shaobo Colonization Agricultural Households.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Silu inherited the post of Commander of the Shaobo Colonization Agricultural Households.

sentences.zh: 思謙，湖廣行省參知政事。

translations.literal: Siquan was Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Siquan served as Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 弟天祥。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tianxiang.

sentences.zh: 天祥字吉甫，因兄祐仕河南，自寧晉徙家洛陽。

translations.literal: Tianxiang, styled Jifu, because his elder brother You served in Henan, moved his family from Ningjin to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang, styled Jifu, moved his family from Ningjin to Luoyang when his elder brother You took office in Henan.

sentences.zh: 天祥少隸軍籍，善騎射。

translations.literal: Tianxiang in his youth was enrolled in military register; he was skilled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Tianxiang was enrolled in the military register and was skilled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮叛據濟南，結宋為外援，河北河南宣慰司承製以天祥為千戶，屯三汊口，防遏宋兵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan, linking with Song for external support. The Pacification Commission of Hebei and Henan, acting on imperial order, appointed Tianxiang as commander of a thousand and stationed him at Sankou to block Song troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhongtong reign, Li Tan rebelled and seized Jinan, seeking Song support from outside. The Pacification Commission of Hebei and Henan, acting on imperial order, appointed Tianxiang commander of a thousand and stationed him at Sankou to block Song forces.

sentences.zh: 事平罷歸，居偃師南山，有田百餘畝，躬耕讀書，從之遊者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was dismissed and returned home. He lived on the southern slopes of Mount Yanshi in Yanshi; he had over a hundred mu of fields, farming and reading himself. Many followed him to study.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed he was dismissed and returned home. He settled on the southern slopes of the mountains in Yanshi, where he owned more than a hundred mu of land, farming and reading by himself. Many came to study with him.

sentences.zh: 其居近緱氏山，因號曰緱山先生。

translations.literal: His residence was near Mount Gou; therefore he took the sobriquet Master of Mount Gou.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay near Mount Gou, and he took the sobriquet Master of Mount Gou.

sentences.zh: 初，天祥未知學，祐未之奇也，別去數歲，獻所為詩於祐，祐疑假手它人，及與語，出入經史，談辨該博，乃大稱異。

translations.literal: At first Tianxiang had not yet pursued learning, and You did not think him remarkable. After they parted for several years, Tianxiang presented poems he had written to You. You suspected someone else had written them; when he conversed with him and found him drawing on the classics and histories with broad and penetrating discussion, he was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tianxiang had not yet devoted himself to learning, and You did not think him especially promising. After they parted for several years, Tianxiang presented poems he had written to You. You suspected they had been written by someone else, but when they spoke together and Tianxiang moved easily through the classics and histories with broad and penetrating discussion, You was greatly astonished.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，起家從仕郎、郢復州等處招討司經歷，從國兵渡江，因論軍中事，深為行省參正賈居貞所器重。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, he began office as Gentleman-of-Service and Manager of the Pacification Commission of E and Fu and other places. Following the imperial army across the Yangzi, he discussed military affairs and was deeply valued by Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat Jia Juzhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan reign, he entered office as Gentleman-of-Service and Manager of the Pacification Commission of E, Fu, and other places. Crossing the Yangzi with the imperial army, he discussed military affairs and won the deep respect of Jia Juzhen, Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十三年，興國軍以籍兵器致亂，行省命天祥權知本軍事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Xingguo Army rebelled over the registration of weapons. The Branch Secretariat ordered Tianxiang to act as temporary military commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, Xingguo Army rebelled over the registration of weapons. The Branch Secretariat ordered Tianxiang to serve temporarily as military commander of the army.

sentences.zh: 天祥領軍士才十人，入其境，去城近百里，止二日乃至城中，父老來謁，天祥諭之曰：「捍衛鄉井，誠不可無兵，任事者籍之過當，故致亂爾。

translations.literal: Tianxiang led only ten soldiers into its territory. Though less than a hundred li from the city, it took two days to reach the city. The elders came to pay respects. Tianxiang instructed them: "Defending one's village truly cannot be done without arms. Those in charge registered them excessively, and so rebellion arose."
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang entered the territory with only ten soldiers. Though less than a hundred li from the city, it took two days to reach it. When the local elders came to pay their respects, Tianxiang told them, "Defending one's home truly cannot be done without arms; those in charge registered weapons excessively, and that is what caused the rebellion."

sentences.zh: 今令汝輩權置兵仗以自衛，何如？

translations.literal: Now I order you provisionally to keep weapons for self-defense—how does that sound?
translations.idiomatic: From now on I will allow you provisionally to keep weapons for self-defense—what do you think of that?

sentences.zh: 」民皆稱便。

translations.literal: " The people all said it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people all said it was a welcome relief.

sentences.zh: 乃條陳其事於行省曰：「鎮遏奸邪，當實根本，若內無備御之資，則外生窺覦之釁，此理勢必然者也。

translations.literal: He then memorialized the Branch Secretariat in detail: "To suppress the wicked, one must strengthen the root. If internally there are no resources for defense, externally there will arise occasions for covetous regard—this is the inevitable logic of circumstance."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a detailed memorial to the Branch Secretariat: "To suppress the wicked, one must strengthen the foundations at home. If there are no means of defense within, occasions for outside covetousness will arise—this is the inevitable logic of the situation."

sentences.zh: 推此軍變亂之故，正由當時處置失宜，疏於外而急於內。

translations.literal: Extrapolating the cause of this army's revolt, it was precisely because at the time the measures were ill-conceived—loose outwardly but strict inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the cause of this army's revolt, it arose precisely because the measures taken at the time were ill-conceived—lax toward the outside but harsh within.

sentences.zh: 凡在軍中者，寸鐵尺杖不得在手，遂使奸人得以竊發，公私同被其害。

translations.literal: All those in the army were forbidden to hold even a finger's length of iron or a foot of staff in hand, so that wicked men could steal the opportunity to rise up, and public and private alike suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the army was forbidden to hold even the smallest weapon in hand, which allowed wicked men to seize the moment to rise up, to the harm of both public and private interests alike.

sentences.zh: 今軍中再經殘破，單弱至此，若猶相防而不相保信，豈惟外寇可憂，第恐舟中之人皆敵國矣。

translations.literal: Now the army has again been battered and weakened to this degree. If they still guard against one another without mutual trust and protection, not only will external enemies be worrisome—I fear those in the same boat will all become enemy states.
translations.idiomatic: Now the army has been battered and weakened to this point. If men still guard against one another instead of trusting and protecting one another, it is not only external enemies that should worry us—I fear those in the same boat will all become enemies.

sentences.zh: 莫若布推赤心於人，使戮力同心，與均禍福，人則我之人，兵則我之兵，靖亂止姦，無施不可。

translations.literal: Better to spread sincere hearts among the people, so that they join in strength with one heart, sharing calamity and blessing alike. The people will be my people; the troops will be my troops—pacifying disorder and stopping wickedness, nothing will be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Better to show sincere hearts to the people, so that they join in strength with one mind and share fortune and misfortune alike. Then the people will be my people and the troops my troops; pacifying disorder and stopping wickedness will become possible in every way.

sentences.zh: 惟冀少加優容，然後責其必成之效。

translations.literal: I only hope for a little indulgence, and then I can demand results that must succeed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask only for a little latitude; then I can be held to results that must succeed.

sentences.zh: 」行省許以從便處置。

translations.literal: " The Branch Secretariat permitted him to act as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat allowed him to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 天祥凡所設施，皆合眾望，由是流移復業，以至鄰郡之民來歸者相繼，伐茅斬木，結屋以居。

translations.literal: Whatever Tianxiang implemented accorded with public expectation. Thereupon displaced persons returned to their occupations; people from neighboring prefectures came to join in succession, cutting thatch and wood to build dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Everything Tianxiang put in place accorded with what the people hoped for. Displaced persons returned to their occupations, and people from neighboring prefectures came in succession, cutting thatch and timber to build homes.

sentences.zh: 天祥命以十家為甲，十甲有長，弛兵禁以從民便。

translations.literal: Tianxiang ordered them organized in groups of ten households as one jia, with a chief over ten jia; he relaxed the prohibition on weapons for the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang organized the people in groups of ten households as one jia, with a chief over every ten jia, and relaxed the ban on weapons for the people's convenience.

sentences.zh: 人心既安，軍勢稍振，用土兵收李必聰山寨，不戮一人。

translations.literal: Once hearts were settled, military strength gradually revived. Using local troops he captured Li Bicong's mountain stronghold without killing a single person.
translations.idiomatic: Once hearts were settled, military strength gradually revived. Using local troops he took Li Bicong's mountain stronghold without killing a single person.

sentences.zh: 他寨聞之，各自散去，境內悉平。

translations.literal: Other strongholds heard of this and dispersed on their own; the entire territory was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Other strongholds heard of this and dispersed on their own, and the entire territory was pacified.

sentences.zh: 時州縣官吏未有俸祿，天祥從便規措而月給之，以止其貪，民用弗擾。

translations.literal: At that time district and county officials had no salaries. Tianxiang improvised arrangements and paid them monthly to check their greed; the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time district and county officials received no salaries. Tianxiang improvised arrangements and paid them monthly to curb their greed, so the people were not harassed.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑分寧為變，諜者時至，吏請捕之，天祥曰：「彼以官吏貪暴故叛，今我一軍三縣，官無侵漁，民樂其業，使之歸告其黨，則諜者反為我用矣。

translations.literal: The neighboring district Fenning rebelled; spies came from time to time. The clerks requested to arrest them. Tianxiang said: "They rebel because officials are greedy and violent. Now in this one army and three districts, officials do not plunder; the people are content in their occupations. Let them return and tell their fellows—and the spies will serve us instead."
translations.idiomatic: The neighboring district of Fenning rebelled, and spies came from time to time. The clerks asked to arrest them. Tianxiang said, "They rebel because officials are greedy and abusive. In this army and its three districts, officials do not plunder and the people are content in their occupations. Let the spies return and report to their fellows, and they will serve us instead."

sentences.zh: 」遂一無所問。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he made no inquiries whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: He made no inquiries at all.

sentences.zh: 及敗，逃入興國境者數千人，天祥命驗口給糧，仍戒土人勿侵陵。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated, several thousand fled into Xingguo territory. Tianxiang ordered them registered and given grain, and warned local people not to molest them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, several thousand fled into Xingguo territory. Tianxiang had them registered and given grain, and warned local people not to molest them.

sentences.zh: 事定，皆得保全而歸，莫不服其威信。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, all were preserved and returned home; none failed to submit to his prestige and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, all were able to return home safely, and none failed to submit to his authority and good faith.

sentences.zh: 居歲餘，詔改本軍為路，有代天祥為總管者，務變更舊政，治隱匿兵者甚急，天祥去未久而興國復變，鄰郡壽昌府及大江南北諸城邑，多乘勢殺守將以應之。

translations.literal: After more than a year, an edict changed this army to a circuit. Someone replaced Tianxiang as chief administrator and zealously changed the old policies, urgently pursuing those who concealed weapons. Tianxiang had not been gone long when Xingguo rebelled again; Shouchang Prefecture in the neighboring district and many towns north and south of the river, seizing the opportunity, killed their garrison commanders to respond.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, an edict changed the army into a circuit. A successor replaced Tianxiang as chief administrator and zealously overturned his old policies, urgently prosecuting those who concealed weapons. Tianxiang had not been gone long when Xingguo rebelled again; Shouchang Prefecture in the neighboring district and many towns north and south of the river seized the moment, killing their garrison commanders in response.

sentences.zh: 時方改行省為宣慰司，參政忽都帖木兒、賈居貞，萬戶鄭鼎臣為宣慰使。

translations.literal: At that time the Branch Secretariat was being changed to a Pacification Commission; Vice Directors Hudutie'mur and Jia Juzhen, and Commander of Ten Thousand Zheng Dingchen served as Pacification Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Branch Secretariat was being converted into a Pacification Commission; Vice Directors Hudutie'mur and Jia Juzhen, together with Commander of Ten Thousand Zheng Dingchen, served as Pacification Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 鼎臣帥兵討之，至樊口，兵敗死。

translations.literal: Dingchen led troops to suppress them. At Fankou the army was defeated and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Dingchen led troops to suppress the rebels, but at Fankou his army was defeated and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 黃州遂聲言攻陽羅堡，鄂州大震。

translations.literal: Huang Prefecture then proclaimed an attack on Yangluo Fort; E Prefecture was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Prefecture then announced an attack on Yangluo Fort, and E Prefecture was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 時忽都帖木兒恇怯不敢出兵，天祥言於居貞曰：「陽羅堡依山為壘，素有嚴備，彼若來攻，我之利也。

translations.literal: At that time Hudutie'mur was cowardly and dared not send troops. Tianxiang said to Juzhen: "Yangluo Fort relies on the mountain for its ramparts and has always had strict defenses. If they come to attack, the advantage is ours."
translations.idiomatic: Hudutie'mur was timid and dared not send out troops. Tianxiang said to Juzhen, "Yangluo Fort is built on the mountain as a rampart and has always been strongly defended. If they come to attack, the advantage will be ours."

sentences.zh: 且南人浮躁，輕進易退，官軍憑高據險，而區區烏合之眾，與之相敵，不二三日，死傷必多，遁逃者十八九，我出精兵以擊之，惟疾走者乃始得脫。

translations.literal: Moreover southerners are impetuous—quick to advance, easy to retreat. Our official troops holding the high ground in a defensible position, matched against a mere rabble—within two or three days casualties will certainly be heavy; eighty or ninety percent will flee. We send elite troops to strike them—only those who run fastest will escape.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, southerners are impetuous—quick to advance and easy to retreat. Our official troops, holding the high ground in a strong position, need only face a mere rabble; within two or three days casualties will be heavy and eight or nine out of ten will flee. Then we send elite troops to strike them, and only the swiftest runners will escape.

sentences.zh: 乘此一勝，則大勢已定。

translations.literal: Seizing this one victory, the greater situation will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: With that one victory, the larger situation will be settled.

sentences.zh: 然後取黃州、壽昌，如摧枯拉朽耳。

translations.literal: Then take Huang Prefecture and Shouchang—as easily as crushing dry wood or pulling rotten fiber.
translations.idiomatic: Then taking Huang Prefecture and Shouchang will be as easy as crushing dry wood or pulling rotten fiber.

sentences.zh: 」居貞深然之，而忽都帖木兒意猶未決。

translations.literal: " Juzhen strongly agreed; but Hudutie'mur's mind was still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Juzhen strongly agreed, but Hudutie'mur still could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 聞至陽羅堡，居貞力趣之，乃引兵宿於青山，明日，大敗其眾，皆如天祥所料。

translations.literal: When word came they had reached Yangluo Fort, Juzhen urgently urged action. They led troops to camp at Qingshan. The next day they thoroughly routed the enemy—all as Tianxiang had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the enemy had reached Yangluo Fort, Juzhen urgently pressed for action. They led troops to camp at Qingshan, and the next day thoroughly routed the enemy—just as Tianxiang had predicted.

sentences.zh: 初，行省聞變，盡執鄂州城中南人將殺之，以防內應，居貞救之不能得，天祥曰：「是州之人，與彼勢本不相接，欲殺之者，利其財耳。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Branch Secretariat heard of the rebellion, they arrested all the southern commanders in E Prefecture city intending to kill them to prevent internal collusion. Juzhen tried to save them but could not. Tianxiang said: "The people of this prefecture have no natural connection with those forces—the reason someone wants to kill them is to seize their wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Branch Secretariat heard of the rebellion, it arrested all the southerners in E Prefecture city and planned to kill them to prevent internal collusion. Juzhen tried to save them but failed. Tianxiang said, "The people of this prefecture have no real connection with the rebels; those who want them killed simply covet their wealth."

sentences.zh: 」力止之，至是被執者皆縱去。

translations.literal: " He vigorously stopped it. When the time came, all those arrested were released.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully stopped the plan, and when the time came all those arrested were released.

sentences.zh: 復遣天祥權知壽昌府事，授兵二百餘人。

translations.literal: Tianxiang was again dispatched to act as temporary administrator of Shouchang Prefecture, granted over two hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang was again dispatched to serve temporarily as administrator of Shouchang Prefecture, with more than two hundred soldiers assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 為亂者聞官軍至，皆棄城依險而自保。

translations.literal: The rebels, hearing official troops had arrived, all abandoned the cities and relied on natural defenses to protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard that official troops had arrived, they all abandoned the cities and took refuge in defensible terrain.

sentences.zh: 天祥以眾寡不敵，非可以力服，乃遣諭其徒使各歸田裡，惟生擒其長毛遇順、周監斬於鄂州市。

translations.literal: Tianxiang, outnumbered, knew he could not subdue them by force. He sent emissaries to instruct their followers to return to their fields, only capturing alive their leaders Mao Yushun and Zhou Jian and executing them in the marketplace of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang knew he was outnumbered and could not subdue them by force alone. He sent envoys to tell their followers to return to their fields, while capturing alive only their leaders Mao Yushun and Zhou Jian and executing them in the marketplace of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 得金二百兩，詢知為鄂州賈人之物，召而還之。

translations.literal: Two hundred taels of gold were obtained; inquiry revealed they belonged to a merchant of E Prefecture. He summoned him and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred taels of gold were recovered; inquiry showed they belonged to a merchant of E Prefecture, and Tianxiang summoned him and returned the gold.

sentences.zh: 其黨王宗一等十三人繼亦就擒，以冬至日放令還家，約三日來歸獄，皆如期而至，白宣慰司盡縱之，由是無復叛者，百姓為立生祠。

translations.literal: Their followers Wang Zongyi and twelve others were also captured in succession. On the winter solstice he released them to go home, arranging for them to return to prison in three days—all arrived on schedule. He reported to the Pacification Commission and they were all released. From then on there were no more rebels; the people erected a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers Wang Zongyi and twelve others were also captured in turn. On the winter solstice he released them to go home, on the understanding that they would return to prison in three days; all arrived on schedule. He reported to the Pacification Commission and they were all released. From then on there were no further rebels, and the people erected a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 二十一年三月，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-first year, he was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-first year, he was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 會右丞盧世榮以掊克聚斂驟升執政，權傾一時。

translations.literal: Just then Right Director Lu Shirong, through extortion and accumulation of wealth, was suddenly elevated to governing power; his authority eclipsed all for a time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Right Director Lu Shirong, who had risen to power through extortion and ruthless enrichment, wielded authority that overshadowed everyone else.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞崔彧言之，帝怒，欲致之法，世榮勢焰益張。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu spoke of this; the emperor was angry and wished to bring him to justice. Shirong's power and arrogance grew all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Supervising Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu spoke out against him, the emperor grew angry and wanted to prosecute him, but Shirong's power and arrogance only grew.

sentences.zh: 左司郎中周ρ因議事微有可否，世榮誣以沮法，奏令杖一百，然後斬之，於是臣僚震懾，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Director of the Left Office Zhou Di, because in deliberating he slightly expressed approval or disapproval, Shirong falsely accused him of obstructing the law and memorialized that he be beaten one hundred strokes and then beheaded. Thereupon the officials were shaken and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Di, Director of the Left Office, had mildly expressed dissent during deliberations. Shirong falsely accused him of obstructing the law and memorialized that he be beaten one hundred strokes and then beheaded. From then on the officials were terrified, and none dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 二十二年四月，天祥上疏，極言世榮奸惡，其略曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year, Tianxiang submitted a memorial strongly denouncing Shirong's wickedness. The gist was as follows:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-second year, Tianxiang submitted a memorial denouncing Shirong's wickedness at length. The gist was as follows:

sentences.zh: 盧世榮素無文藝，亦無武功，惟以商販所獲之貲，趨附權臣，營求入仕，輿贓輦賄，輸送權門，所獻不充，又別立欠少文券銀一千錠，由白身擢江西榷茶轉運使。

translations.literal: Lu Shirong from the first had no literary accomplishment and no military merit. He relied only on wealth gained from trade, currying favor with powerful ministers and scheming to enter office. He carted bribes and conveyed gifts to the gates of power; when what he offered was insufficient, he additionally drew up a debt note for one thousand ingots of silver. From commoner status he was promoted to Transport Commissioner for the Jiangxi Tea Monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shirong had no literary accomplishment and no military merit. He relied solely on wealth gained from trade, currying favor with powerful ministers to enter office. He carted bribes to the gates of power, and when his gifts fell short he even drew up a debt note for one thousand ingots of silver. From commoner status he was promoted to Transport Commissioner for the Jiangxi Tea Monopoly.

sentences.zh: 於其任，專務貪饕，所犯贓私，動以萬計。

translations.literal: In his post he devoted himself solely to greed; the embezzlement and private gain he committed amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In office he devoted himself solely to greed, and the embezzlement and private gain he committed ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 其隱秘者固難悉舉，惟發露者乃可明言，凡其掊取於人及所盜官物，略計：鈔以錠計者二萬五千一百一十九，金以錠計者二十五，銀以錠計者一百六十八，茶以引計者一萬二千四百五十有八，馬以匹計者十五，玉器七事，其餘繁雜物件稱是。

translations.literal: What was concealed is naturally hard to enumerate fully; only what was exposed can be stated clearly. In total, what he extorted from others and stole from official property, roughly counted: paper money in ingot units, 25,119; gold in ingot units, 25; silver in ingot units, 168; tea in certificate units, 12,458; horses in head units, 15; jade objects, seven items; other miscellaneous objects in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: What he concealed cannot all be listed, but what was exposed can be stated plainly. Roughly counted, what he extorted from others and stole from official property included: 25,119 ingots of paper money, 25 ingots of gold, 168 ingots of silver, 12,458 tea certificates, 15 horses, seven jade objects, and a comparable assortment of other goods.

sentences.zh: 已經追納及未納見追者，人所共知。

translations.literal: What had already been recovered and what remained unpaid and was still being pursued—all knew of this.
translations.idiomatic: What had already been recovered and what remained unpaid and was still being pursued were common knowledge.

sentences.zh: 今竟不悔前非，狂悖愈甚，以苛刻為自安之策，以誅求為乾進之門，既懷無饜之心，廣畜攘掊之計，而又身當要路，手握重權，雖位在丞相之下，朝省大政，實得專之。

translations.literal: Now he still does not repent his former wrongs; his arrogance grows ever worse. He takes harshness as his policy of self-preservation and exaction as his path to advancement. Already harboring insatiable ambition, he broadly stores schemes of plunder. Moreover he stands on a crucial path and holds heavy authority; though his rank is below the chief counselor, in fact he monopolizes the great affairs of court and secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Now he still shows no repentance for his past wrongs, and his arrogance grows worse. He treats harshness as a policy of self-preservation and exaction as a path to advancement. Insatiable in ambition, he hoards schemes of plunder. Standing at a crucial post and wielding heavy authority, though his rank is below the chief counselor, he in fact monopolizes the great affairs of court and secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是猶以盜跖而掌阿衡之任，不止流殃於當代，亦恐取笑於將來。

translations.literal: This is like putting a robber in charge of the office of prime minister—not only will calamity flow to the present age, but I fear he will become a laughingstock to future generations.
translations.idiomatic: This is like putting a robber in charge of the prime ministership—not only will calamity afflict the present age, but I fear he will become a laughingstock to posterity.

sentences.zh: 朝廷信其虛誑之說，俾居相位，名為試驗，實授正權。

translations.literal: The court believed his false and deceitful words and had him occupy the chief counselor's position—called a trial, but in fact granting full authority.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed his false and deceitful claims and placed him in the chief counselor's position—called a trial, but in fact granting him full authority.

sentences.zh: 校其所能，敗闕如此；

translations.literal: Examining what he could do, his failures were such as this;
translations.idiomatic: Judging what he could do, his failures were already plain;

sentences.zh: 考其所行，毫髮無稱。

translations.literal: examining what he had done, not even the smallest part was praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: examining what he had done, not even the smallest part was praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 此皆既往之真跡，可謂已試之明驗。

translations.literal: These are all true traces of what has passed; they can be called clear proof already tested.
translations.idiomatic: These are all established facts of the past and clear proof already tested.

sentences.zh: 若謂必須再試，止可敘以他官，宰相之權，豈宜輕授。

translations.literal: If one says he must be tested again, he should be appointed only to another office. The authority of chief counselor—how can it be lightly granted?
translations.idiomatic: If he must be tested again, he should be appointed only to another office. The authority of chief counselor should not be granted lightly.

sentences.zh: 夫宰天下，譬猶制錦。

translations.literal: Governing all under Heaven is like weaving brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Governing all under Heaven is like weaving brocade.

sentences.zh: 初欲驗其能否，先當試以布帛，如無能效，所損或輕。

translations.literal: If at first one wishes to test ability, one should first try cloth and silk; if there is no effect, the loss may be slight.
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes first to test ability, one should begin with cloth and silk; if there is no success, the loss may be slight.

sentences.zh: 今捐相位以試驗賢愚，猶舍美錦以校量工拙，脫致隳壞，悔將何追！

translations.literal: Now to discard the chief counselor's position to test wise and foolish is like abandoning fine brocade to measure skill and clumsiness. If ruin results, what regret can make amends!
translations.idiomatic: Now to use the chief counselor's position to test wise and foolish men is like abandoning fine brocade to measure skill and clumsiness. If ruin follows, what regret can make amends!

sentences.zh: 國家之與百姓，上下如同一身，民乃國之血氣，國乃民之膚體。

translations.literal: The state and the common people, above and below, are like one body: the people are the state's blood and breath; the state is the people's skin and flesh.
translations.idiomatic: The state and the common people, above and below, are like one body: the people are the state's blood and breath, and the state is the people's skin and flesh.

sentences.zh: 血氣充實則膚體康強，血氣損傷則膚體羸病。

translations.literal: When blood and breath are full, the skin and flesh are strong and healthy; when blood and breath are injured, the skin and flesh grow weak and sick.
translations.idiomatic: When blood and breath are full, the skin and flesh are strong and healthy; when blood and breath are injured, the skin and flesh grow weak and sick.

sentences.zh: 未有耗其血氣能使膚體豐榮者。

translations.literal: Never has exhausting the blood and breath made the skin and flesh flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Never has exhausting the blood and breath made the skin and flesh flourish.

sentences.zh: 是故民富則國富，民貧則國貧，民安則國安，民困則國困，其理然也。

translations.literal: Therefore when the people are rich, the state is rich; when the people are poor, the state is poor; when the people are secure, the state is secure; when the people are distressed, the state is distressed—such is the logic.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the people are rich, the state is rich; when the people are poor, the state is poor; when the people are secure, the state is secure; when the people are distressed, the state is distressed. Such is the logic of the matter.

sentences.zh: 昔魯哀公欲重斂於民，問於有若，對曰：「百姓足，君敦與不足；

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Ai of Lu wished to levy heavily on the people and asked You Ruo. He replied: "When the common people have enough, how can the lord not have enough?"
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Ai of Lu wished to levy heavily on the people and asked You Ruo, who replied, "When the common people have enough, how can the lord not have enough?"

sentences.zh: 百姓不足，君孰與足？

translations.literal: When the common people do not have enough, with whom will the lord have enough?
translations.idiomatic: When the common people do not have enough, with whom will the lord have enough?"

sentences.zh: 」以此推之，民必須賦輕而後足，國必待民足而後豐。

translations.literal: " From this one infers: the people must have light levies before they can have enough; the state must wait for the people to have enough before it can be abundant.
translations.idiomatic: From this one infers that the people must have light levies before they can prosper, and the state must wait for the people to prosper before it can be abundant.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「民為邦本，本固邦寧。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is secure."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, "The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is secure."

sentences.zh: 」歷考前代，因百姓富安以致亂，百姓困窮以致治，自有天地以來，未之聞也。

translations.literal: " Examining former ages, that disorder came because the common people were rich and secure, or that order came because the common people were distressed and impoverished—since Heaven and Earth began, one has never heard of this.
translations.idiomatic: Examining former ages, one has never heard since Heaven and Earth began of disorder arising because the common people were rich and secure, or of order arising because the common people were distressed and impoverished.

sentences.zh: 夫財者，土地所生，民力所集，天地之間歲有常數，惟其取之有節，故其用之不乏。

translations.literal: Wealth is what the land produces and what the people's labor gathers. Between Heaven and Earth there is a fixed annual measure; only when taking is regulated is use not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth is what the land produces and what the people's labor gathers. Between Heaven and Earth there is a fixed annual measure; only when taking is regulated is use not exhausted.

sentences.zh: 今世榮欲以一歲之期，將致十年之積；

translations.literal: Now Shirong wishes in the space of one year to produce ten years' accumulation;
translations.idiomatic: Now Shirong wishes in the space of one year to produce ten years' accumulation;

sentences.zh: 危萬民之命，易一世之榮；

translations.literal: endangering the lives of ten thousand people, exchanging one generation's glory;
translations.idiomatic: endangering the lives of countless people for the sake of one generation's glory;

sentences.zh: 廣邀增羨之功，不恤顛連之患；

translations.literal: broadly inviting credit for increased surplus, not caring for the calamity of the destitute and afflicted;
translations.idiomatic: broadly inviting credit for increased revenue, heedless of the calamity of the destitute and afflicted;

sentences.zh: 期錙銖之誅取，誘上下以交徵。

translations.literal: expecting exaction down to the smallest measure, inducing above and below to levy on one another.
translations.idiomatic: expecting exaction down to the smallest measure and inducing above and below to levy on one another.

sentences.zh: 視民如讎，為國斂怨。

translations.literal: He treats the people as enemies and accumulates resentment for the state.
translations.idiomatic: He treats the people as enemies and accumulates resentment for the state.

sentences.zh: 果慾不為國家之遠慮，惟取速效於目前，肆意誅求，何所不得。

translations.literal: If he truly does not care for the state's long-term planning and seeks only quick results before his eyes, then by exaction as he pleases, what could he not obtain?
translations.idiomatic: If he truly does not care for the state's long-term planning and seeks only quick results before his eyes, then by exaction as he pleases, what could he not obtain?

sentences.zh: 然其生財之本既已不存，斂財之方復何所賴？

translations.literal: Yet if the root of producing wealth no longer exists, on what can the method of gathering wealth rely?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the root of producing wealth no longer exists, on what can the method of gathering wealth rely?

sentences.zh: 將見民間由此凋耗，天下由此空虛，安危利害之機，殆有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: One will see the populace thereby wither and waste, all under Heaven thereby become empty; the turning points of security and danger, benefit and harm—there are likely matters beyond what can be fully told.
translations.idiomatic: One will see the populace wither and waste, and all under Heaven grow empty; the turning points of security and danger, benefit and harm, are likely beyond what can fully be told.

sentences.zh: 計其任事以來，百有餘日，驗其事蹟，備有顯明。

translations.literal: Counting from when he took office, there have been over a hundred days; examining his deeds, all are clearly evident.
translations.idiomatic: Counting from when he took office, more than a hundred days have passed, and examining his deeds, the evidence is clear.

sentences.zh: 今取其所行與所言而已不相副者，略舉數端：始言能令鈔法如舊，鈔今愈虛；

translations.literal: Now taking what he has done and what he said that already do not match, I briefly cite several instances: at first he said he could make the paper-money system as before—paper money is now more debased;
translations.idiomatic: Taking what he has done and what he said that already do not match, I briefly cite several instances: at first he said he could restore the paper-money system as before, yet paper money is now more debased;

sentences.zh: 始言能令百物自賤，物今愈貴；

translations.literal: at first he said he could make all goods cheapen themselves—goods are now more expensive;
translations.idiomatic: at first he said he could make all goods cheapen themselves, yet goods are now more expensive;

sentences.zh: 始言課程增添三百萬錠，不取於民而辦，今卻迫脅諸路官司增數包認；

translations.literal: at first he said revenue could be increased by three million ingots without taking from the people—now he coerces the circuit offices to increase quotas and accept responsibility;
translations.idiomatic: at first he said revenue could be increased by three million ingots without taking from the people, yet now he coerces the circuit offices to increase quotas and accept responsibility;

sentences.zh: 始言能令民快樂，凡今所為，無非敗法擾民者。

translations.literal: at first he said he could make the people happy—everything done now is nothing but violating law and disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: at first he said he could make the people happy, yet everything done now is nothing but violating law and disturbing the people.

sentences.zh: 若不早有更張，須其自敗，正猶蠹雖除去，木病亦深，始嫌曲突徙薪，終見焦頭爛額，事至於此，救將何及？

translations.literal: If one does not early make changes and waits for him to fail on his own, it is just like removing the worm but the tree's disease is already deep—at first one dislikes bending the chimney and moving the firewood, but in the end one sees scorched head and burned brow. When matters reach this point, what rescue can there be in time?
translations.idiomatic: If one does not make changes early and waits for him to fail on his own, it is like removing the worm while the tree's disease is already deep—at first one dislikes bending the chimney and moving the firewood, but in the end one sees scorched head and burned brow. When matters reach this point, what rescue can there be in time?

sentences.zh: 臣亦知阿附權要則榮寵可期，違忤重臣則禍患難測，緘默自固，亦豈不能！

translations.literal: Your subject also knows that currying favor with the powerful brings expected honor and favor, while opposing great ministers makes disaster hard to foretell. To keep silent and secure oneself—could one not do that!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject also knows that currying favor with the powerful brings expected honor and favor, while opposing great ministers makes disaster hard to foretell. To keep silent and secure oneself—could one not do that!

sentences.zh: 正以事在國家，關係不淺，憂深慮切，不得無言。

translations.literal: It is precisely because the matter concerns the state and the connection is not shallow that, with deep worry and urgent concern, one cannot remain silent.
translations.idiomatic: It is precisely because the matter concerns the state and the stakes are high that, with deep worry and urgent concern, I cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞其語，遣使召天祥與世榮，俱至上都面質之。

translations.literal: Kublai heard his words and dispatched envoys to summon Tianxiang and Shirong; both went to Shangdu to confront one another face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai heard his words and dispatched envoys to summon Tianxiang and Shirong; both went to Shangdu to confront one another face to face.

sentences.zh: 既至，即日有內官傳旨，縛世榮於宮門外。

translations.literal: When they arrived, that very day an inner palace official transmitted an edict and bound Shirong outside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, that very day an inner palace official transmitted an edict and bound Shirong outside the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 明日入對，天祥於帝前再舉其所言與未及盡言者，帝皆稱善，世榮遂伏誅。

translations.literal: The next day he entered audience. Before the emperor Tianxiang again presented what he had said and what he had not yet fully said; the emperor praised it all. Shirong was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he entered audience. Before the emperor Tianxiang again presented what he had said and what he had not yet fully said; the emperor praised it all, and Shirong was executed.

sentences.zh: 五月，朝廷錄天祥從軍渡江及平興國、壽昌之功，進秩五品，擢吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the court recorded Tianxiang's merit in following the army across the Yangzi and pacifying Xingguo and Shouchang. His rank was advanced to fifth grade and he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the court recorded Tianxiang's merit in following the army across the Yangzi and pacifying Xingguo and Shouchang. His rank was advanced to fifth grade and he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十三年四月，除治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 六月，命理算湖北湖南行省錢糧。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he was ordered to audit the funds and grain of the Hubei and Hunan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, he was ordered to audit the funds and grain of the Hubei and Hunan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天祥至鄂州，即上疏劾平章岳束木凶暴不法。

translations.literal: When Tianxiang reached E Prefecture, he immediately submitted a memorial impeaching Vice Director Yue Shumu for violence and lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiang reached E Prefecture, he immediately submitted a memorial impeaching Vice Director Yue Shumu for violence and lawlessness.

sentences.zh: 時桑哥竊國柄，與岳束木姻黨，為其爪牙羽翼，誣天祥以罪，欲致之死，繫獄幾四百日。

translations.literal: At the time Sangge usurped state power; he was related by marriage to Yue Shumu and served as his claws and wings. He falsely accused Tianxiang of crimes and wished to bring him to death; he was imprisoned for nearly four hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sangge usurped state power. Related by marriage to Yue Shumu, he served as his henchman and falsely accused Tianxiang of crimes, seeking to have him killed. Tianxiang was imprisoned for nearly four hundred days.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春正月，遇赦得釋。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-fifth year, he encountered an amnesty and was released.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the twenty-fifth year, he was released under an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，擢行台侍御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was promoted to Censor of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, he was promoted to Censor of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾辭歸。

translations.literal: Before long, on grounds of illness he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授燕南河北道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he was appointed Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Yannan Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, he was appointed Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Yannan Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，改山東西道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, he was changed to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Shandong East and West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanzhen reign, he was reassigned as Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Shandong East and West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊群起，山東居多，詔求弭盜方略。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in groups, mostly in Shandong. An edict sought strategies to suppress banditry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits rose in groups, mostly in Shandong, and an edict sought strategies to suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 天祥上奏曰：「古者盜賊之起，各有所因，除歲凶饑饉，諉之天時，宜且勿論。

translations.literal: Tianxiang memorialized: "In antiquity when bandits arose, each had its cause. Apart from years of disaster and famine, which may be attributed to Heaven's seasons and need not be discussed for now—
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang memorialized, "In antiquity when bandits arose, each case had its cause. Apart from years of disaster and famine, which may be attributed to Heaven's seasons and need not be discussed for now,

sentences.zh: 他如軍旅不息，工役薦興，聚斂無厭，刑法紊亂之類，此皆群盜所起之因。

translations.literal: other causes such as unceasing military campaigns, repeated labor corvée, insatiable accumulation of wealth, and disordered punishments—these are all causes from which bandit gangs arise."
translations.idiomatic: other causes such as unceasing military campaigns, repeated labor corvée, insatiable accumulation of wealth, and disordered punishments—these are all causes from which bandit gangs arise."

sentences.zh: 中間保護存卹長養之者，赦令是也。

translations.literal: Among the measures that in the meantime protect, preserve, and nurture them, amnesty edicts are one.
translations.idiomatic: Among the measures that in the meantime protect, preserve, and nurture them, amnesty edicts are one.

sentences.zh: 赦者，小人之幸，君子之不幸。

translations.literal: Amnesty is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty is the petty man's good fortune and the gentleman's misfortune.

sentences.zh: 一歲再赦，善人喑啞，前人言之備矣。

translations.literal: Two amnesties in one year leave good people mute; former men have spoken fully of this.
translations.idiomatic: Two amnesties in one year leave good people mute; former men have spoken fully of this.

sentences.zh: 彼強梁之徒，各執兵杖，殺人取貨，不顧其生，有司盡力以擒之，朝廷加恩以釋之。

translations.literal: Those violent men, each wielding weapons, killing people and seizing goods without regard for their lives—the officials exhaust themselves to capture them, and the court adds grace to release them.
translations.idiomatic: Those violent men, each wielding weapons, killing people and seizing goods without regard for their lives—the officials exhaust themselves to capture them, and the court adds grace to release them.

sentences.zh: 旦脫縲囚，暮即行劫，又復督勒有司，結限追捕。

translations.literal: In the morning they escape the bonds of prison; by evening they are robbing again. Then the court again presses the officials, setting deadlines for pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the morning they escape the bonds of prison; by evening they are robbing again. Then the court again presses the officials, setting deadlines for pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊皆經慣，習以為常，既不感恩，又不畏法，凶殘悖逆，性已頑定。

translations.literal: The bandits have all grown accustomed; they take it as routine. They neither feel gratitude nor fear the law; their violent, cruel, and rebellious nature is already set.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits have all grown accustomed and take it as routine. They neither feel gratitude nor fear the law; their violent, cruel, and rebellious nature is already set.

sentences.zh: 誠非善化能移，惟以嚴刑可製。

translations.literal: Truly they cannot be moved by good transformation; only strict punishment can restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: They truly cannot be moved by good transformation; only strict punishment can restrain them.

sentences.zh: 」所擬事條，皆切於時用。

translations.literal: " The proposed measures were all suited to present needs.
translations.idiomatic: The proposed measures were all suited to present needs.

sentences.zh: 於是嚴督有司，捕得盜賊甚眾，皆杖殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he strictly supervised the officials; many bandits were captured and all were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he strictly supervised the officials; many bandits were captured and all were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 其亡入他境者，揣知所向，選捕盜官及弓兵，密授方略，示以賞罰，使追捕之，南至漢、江，二千餘里，悉皆就擒，無得免者。

translations.literal: Those who fled into other territories—he inferred where they were headed, selected bandit-capture officials and archer troops, secretly gave them strategy, showed them rewards and punishments, and had them pursue. South to the Han and Yangzi, over two thousand li, all were captured; none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled into other territories—he inferred where they were headed, selected bandit-capture officials and archer troops, secretly gave them strategy, showed them rewards and punishments, and had them pursue. South to the Han and Yangzi, over two thousand li, all were captured; none escaped.

sentences.zh: 由是東方群盜屏息。

translations.literal: Thereby the bandit gangs of the east fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the bandit gangs of the east fell silent.

sentences.zh: 平陰縣女子劉金蓮，假妖術以惑眾，所至官為建立神堂，愚民皆奔走奉事之，天祥謂同僚曰：「此婦以神怪惑眾，聲勢如此，若復有狡獪之人輔翼之，仿漢張角、晉孫恩之為，必成大害。

translations.literal: Liu Jinlian, a woman of Pingyin County, used false sorcery to delude the masses. Wherever she went officials built spirit halls for her; foolish people all rushed to serve her. Tianxiang said to his colleagues: "This woman uses spirits and marvels to delude the masses; her influence is such that if crafty men again assist her, imitating the deeds of Zhang Jiao of Han and Sun En of Jin, she will surely become a great calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jinlian, a woman of Pingyin County, used false sorcery to delude the masses. Wherever she went officials built spirit halls for her, and foolish people rushed to serve her. Tianxiang said to his colleagues, "This woman uses spirits and marvels to delude the masses; her influence is such that if crafty men assist her, imitating the deeds of Zhang Jiao of Han and Sun En of Jin, she will surely become a great calamity."

sentences.zh: 」遂命捕係而杖於市，自此神聖屏息。

translations.literal: " He then ordered her captured, bound, and beaten in the marketplace. From then on spirit cults fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered her captured, bound, and beaten in the marketplace. From then on spirit cults fell silent.

sentences.zh: 天祥言山東宣慰司官冗宜罷，因劾奏其使貪暴不法，事格不行，遂以任滿辭去。

translations.literal: Tianxiang said the Shandong Pacification Commission had redundant officials that should be abolished, and memorialized impeachment of its commissioner for greed, violence, and lawlessness. The matter was blocked and not carried out; he therefore resigned when his term ended.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang said the Shandong Pacification Commission had redundant officials that should be abolished, and memorialized impeachment of its commissioner for greed, violence, and lawlessness. The matter was blocked and not carried out, and he resigned when his term ended.

sentences.zh: 大德三年六月，遷河北河南廉訪使，以疾不起。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Dade, he was transferred to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for Hebei and Henan, but on grounds of illness did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of the Dade reign, he was transferred to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for Hebei and Henan, but on grounds of illness did not take office.

sentences.zh: 人有冤抑，往往就天祥家求直，天祥以不在其位，卻去之。

translations.literal: People with grievances often came to Tianxiang's home seeking justice. Tianxiang, because he was not in the relevant post, sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: People with grievances often came to Tianxiang's home seeking justice, but he, not holding the relevant post, sent them away.

sentences.zh: 六年，升江南行台御史中丞，上章論征西南夷事，曰：

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was promoted to Supervising Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and submitted a memorial discussing the campaign against the southwestern barbarians, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he was promoted to Supervising Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and submitted a memorial discussing the campaign against the southwestern barbarians, saying:

sentences.zh: 兵有不得已而不已者，亦有得已而不已者。

translations.literal: There is warfare that cannot be stopped though one wishes to stop, and there is warfare that could be stopped yet is not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: There is warfare that cannot be stopped though one wishes to stop, and there is warfare that could be stopped yet is not stopped.

sentences.zh: 惟能得已則已，可使兵力永強，以備不得已而不已之用，是之謂善用兵者也。

translations.literal: Only when one can stop, then stop, can military strength remain forever strong, to prepare for use when stopping is impossible—this is called one who uses troops well.
translations.idiomatic: Only when one can stop, then stop, can military strength remain forever strong, to prepare for use when stopping is impossible—this is what it means to use troops well.

sentences.zh: 去歲，行省右丞劉深遠征八百媳婦國，此乃得已而不已之兵也。

translations.literal: Last year, Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat Liu Shen made a distant expedition against the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives—this is warfare that could be stopped yet was not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat Liu Shen made a distant expedition against the Kingdom of Eight Hundred Wives—this is warfare that could be stopped yet was not stopped.

sentences.zh: 彼荒裔小邦，遠在雲南之西南又數千里，其地為僻陋無用之地，人皆頑愚無知。

translations.literal: That remote small state lies thousands of li beyond Yunnan to the southwest. Its land is remote, crude, and useless; its people are all stubborn, foolish, and ignorant.
translations.idiomatic: That remote small state lies thousands of li beyond Yunnan to the southwest. Its land is remote, crude, and useless; its people are stubborn, foolish, and ignorant.

sentences.zh: 取之不足以為利，不取不足以為害。

translations.literal: Taking it is insufficient to bring benefit; not taking it is insufficient to bring harm.
translations.idiomatic: Taking it would bring no benefit; not taking it would bring no harm.

sentences.zh: 深欺上罔下，帥兵伐之，經過八番，縱橫自恣，恃其威力，虐害居民，中途變生，所在皆叛。

translations.literal: Shen deceived his superiors and misled his subordinates, leading troops to attack it. Passing through the Eight Fan, he acted with unchecked license, relying on his power to abuse and harm the residents. Midway rebellion arose; everywhere all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Shen deceived his superiors and misled his subordinates and led troops to attack it. Passing through the Eight Fan, he acted with unchecked license, relying on his power to abuse and harm the residents. Midway rebellion arose, and everywhere people rebelled.

sentences.zh: 深既不能制亂，反為亂​​眾所製，軍中乏糧，人自相食，計窮勢蹙，倉黃退走，土兵隨擊，以致大敗。

translations.literal: Shen could neither control the disorder nor was instead controlled by the rebellious masses. The army lacked grain; men ate one another. Plans exhausted, situation pressed, he fled in panic. Local troops pursued and struck, leading to great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shen could neither control the disorder nor was instead controlled by the rebels. The army lacked grain and men ate one another. Plans exhausted and the situation desperate, he fled in panic. Local troops pursued and struck, leading to great defeat.

sentences.zh: 深棄眾奔逃，僅以身免，喪兵十八九，棄地千餘里。

translations.literal: Shen abandoned the masses and fled; he barely escaped with his life. Eight or nine tenths of the troops were lost; over a thousand li of territory were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shen abandoned his troops and fled, barely escaping with his life. Eight or nine tenths of the troops were lost, and over a thousand li of territory were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 朝廷再發陝西、河南、江西、湖廣四省諸軍，使劉二霸都總督，以圖收復叛地。

translations.literal: The court again dispatched troops from the four provinces of Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, and Huguang, making Liu Erbadu overall commander, to seek recovery of the rebel territory.
translations.idiomatic: The court again dispatched troops from the four provinces of Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, and Huguang, making Liu Erbadu overall commander, to seek recovery of the rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 湖北、湖南大起丁夫，運送軍糧，至播州交納，其正夫與擔負自己糧食者，通計二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Hubei and Hunan massively conscripted laborers to transport military grain, delivering it at Bozhou. Regular laborers together with those carrying their own grain totaled over two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei and Hunan massively conscripted laborers to transport military grain, delivering it at Bozhou. Regular laborers together with those carrying their own grain totaled over two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 正當農時，興此大役，驅愁苦之人，往回數千里中，何事不有！

translations.literal: Just at farming season this great labor was raised, driving distressed people back and forth over several thousand li—what could not happen!
translations.idiomatic: Just at farming season this great labor was raised, driving distressed people back and forth over several thousand li—what could not happen!

sentences.zh: 或所負之米盡到，固為幸矣。

translations.literal: If the rice they carried all arrived, that would already be fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: If the rice they carried all arrived, that would already be fortunate.

sentences.zh: 然數万之軍，止仰今次一運之米，自此以後，又當如何？」

translations.literal: Yet tens of thousands of troops rely only on this one transport of rice—after this, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet tens of thousands of troops rely only on this one transport of rice—after this, what then?"

sentences.zh: 比問西征敗卒及其將校，頗知西南遠夷之地，重山复嶺，陡澗深林，竹木叢茂，皆有長刺。

translations.literal: Recently I questioned defeated soldiers of the western expedition and their officers; they know something of the remote southwestern barbarian lands: layered mountains and overlapping ridges, steep ravines and deep forests, dense bamboo and trees—all with long thorns.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I questioned defeated soldiers of the western expedition and their officers; they know something of the remote southwestern barbarian lands: layered mountains and overlapping ridges, steep ravines and deep forests, dense bamboo and trees—all with long thorns.

sentences.zh: 軍行徑路在於其間，窄處僅容一人一騎，上如登天，下如入井，賊若乘險邀擊，我軍雖眾，亦難施為也。

translations.literal: The army's paths lie among them; in narrow places only one man or one horse can pass. Going up is like climbing to Heaven; going down is like entering a well. If bandits exploit the terrain to ambush, though our army is numerous, it is hard to act.
translations.idiomatic: The army's paths lie among them; in narrow places only one man or one horse can pass. Going up is like climbing to Heaven; going down is like entering a well. If bandits exploit the terrain to ambush, though our army is numerous, it is hard to act.

sentences.zh: 又其毒霧煙瘴之氣，皆能傷人，群蠻既知大軍將至，若皆清野遠遁，阻其要害，以老我師，或進不得前，旁無所掠，士卒飢餒，疫病死亡，將有不戰自困之勢，不可不為深慮也。
