translations.idiomatic: Shanfu's son Conglong served up to Investigating Censor of the Southern Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 從德，江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: Congde was Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Congde served as Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: ○趙與蒨

translations.literal: ○ Zhao Yuqian
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuqian

sentences.zh: 趙與蒨，字晦叔，宋宗室子，嘗登進士第，為鄂州教授。

translations.literal: Zhao Yuqian, styled Huishu, was a son of the Song imperial clan. He once passed the jinshi examination and served as Instructor of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuqian, styled Huishu, was a member of the Song imperial clan. He had passed the jinshi examination and served as Instructor of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，丞相伯顏既渡江，與蒨率其宗人之在鄂州者，詣軍門上書，力陳不嗜殺人可以一天下，且乞全其宗黨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, after Chief Counselor Bayan had crossed the Yangzi, Yuqian led the clansmen of his house who were in E Prefecture to the army gate to submit a memorial, forcefully stating that not loving killing could unify all under Heaven, and also begging that his clan be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Zhiyuan reign, after Chief Counselor Bayan had crossed the Yangzi, Yuqian led the clansmen of his house who were in E Prefecture to the army gate to submit a memorial, forcefully arguing that refraining from bloodshed could unify all under Heaven, and also begging that his clan be preserved.

sentences.zh: 後伯顏朝京師，世祖問宋宗室之賢者，伯顏首以與蒨對。

translations.literal: Later when Bayan came to court at the capital, Kublai asked about worthy men among the Song imperial clan; Bayan first named Yuqian in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Bayan came to court at the capital, Kublai asked about worthy men among the Song imperial clan, and Bayan first named Yuqian.

sentences.zh: 十三年秋九月，遣使召至上京，幅巾深衣以見，言宋敗亡之故，悉由誤用權奸，詞旨激切，令人感動。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn of the thirteenth year, envoys were dispatched to summon him to Shangdu. Wearing a wide cloth headband and deep robes he had audience, speaking of the causes of Song's defeat and fall—all from mistakenly employing powerful scoundrels. His words were sharp and urgent, moving people.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn of the thirteenth year, envoys were dispatched to summon him to Shangdu. Wearing a scholar's wide cloth headband and deep robes he had audience, speaking of the causes of Song's defeat and fall—all from mistakenly employing powerful scoundrels. His words were sharp and urgent, and deeply moving.

sentences.zh: 世祖念之，即授翰林待制。

translations.literal: Kublai thought of him and immediately appointed him Attending Draftsman of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was impressed and immediately appointed him Attending Draftsman of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷立法，多所諮訪，與蒨忠言讜論，無所顧惜。

translations.literal: When the court established laws, it often consulted him; Yuqian offered loyal and forthright opinions without any reservation.
translations.idiomatic: When the court established laws, it often consulted him; Yuqian offered loyal and forthright opinions without reservation.

sentences.zh: 進直學士，轉侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Academician and transferred to Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Academician and transferred to Lecturer-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 疏陳江南科斂急督，移括大姓，宋世丘壟暴露，皆大臣擅易明詔所為。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated that in Jiangnan levies were urgently pressed, great clans were moved and registered, and Song-era tombs and mounds were exposed—all done by great ministers who on their own authority altered clear edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he stated that in Jiangnan levies were urgently pressed, great clans were moved and registered, and Song-era tombs and mounds were exposed—all done by great ministers who on their own authority altered clear edicts.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，京師霧四塞；

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, fog filled the capital on all sides;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, fog filled the capital on all sides;

sentences.zh: 明年正月甲寅，虎入南城。

translations.literal: in the first month of the next year, on the day jiayin, a tiger entered the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: in the first month of the next year, on the day jiayin, a tiger entered the southern city.

sentences.zh: 與蒨又疏言權臣專正之咎，退而家居待罪。

translations.literal: Yuqian again memorialized on the fault of powerful ministers monopolizing governance, then retired and stayed home awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqian again memorialized on the fault of powerful ministers monopolizing governance, then retired and stayed home awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 未幾桑哥敗，平章不忽木奏與蒨貧窶有守，有抱負，世祖曰：「得非指權臣為虎者邪？

translations.literal: Before long Sangge fell. Vice Director Buqumu memorialized that Yuqian, though poor, had integrity and ambition. Kublai said: "Could this not be the one who called powerful ministers tigers?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sangge fell. Vice Director Buqumu memorialized that Yuqian, though poor, had integrity and ambition. Kublai said, "Could this not be the one who called powerful ministers tigers?"

sentences.zh: 」錫鈔萬三千貫，歲給其妻子衣糧。

translations.literal: " He bestowed thirteen thousand strings of paper money and annually supplied his wife and children with clothing and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed thirteen thousand strings of paper money and annually supplied his wife and children with clothing and grain.

sentences.zh: 後累遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly promoted to Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose to Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 其伯祖師淵，嘗從硃熹學，家庭受授，具有端緒，於是與許衡論尹洛閫奧，衡雅敬之。

translations.literal: His granduncle Shi Yuan had once studied with Zhu Xi; instruction received in the family had clear beginnings and threads. Thereupon he discussed with Xu Heng the inner mysteries of the Cheng-Yi and Luoyang schools; Heng deeply respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His granduncle Shi Yuan had once studied with Zhu Xi, and instruction received in the family had clear foundations. Thereupon he discussed with Xu Heng the inner mysteries of the Cheng-Yi and Luoyang schools, and Heng deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 與蒨既老，成宗命特官其子孟實以終養。

translations.literal: When Yuqian had grown old, Chengzong ordered his son Mengshi specially appointed to office so he could complete his filial care.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqian had grown old, Chengzong ordered his son Mengshi specially appointed to office so he could complete his filial care.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Dade reign, he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以為葬，成宗命有司賻鈔五千貫，給舟軍，還葬台州之黃岩。

translations.literal: The family was poor and had no means for burial. Chengzong ordered the officials to grant five thousand strings of paper money as funeral aid, provide boats and troops, and return him for burial at Huangyan in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor and had no means for burial. Chengzong ordered the officials to grant five thousand strings of paper money as funeral aid, provide boats and troops, and return him for burial at Huangyan in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 贈通議大夫、禮部尚書、上輕車都尉、天水郡侯，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Tongyi Doctor, Minister of Rites, Senior Commandant of Chariots, and Marquis of Tianshui Commandery with the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Tongyi Doctor, Minister of Rites, Senior Commandant of Chariots, and Marquis of Tianshui Commandery with the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: ○姚天福

translations.literal: ○ Yao Tianfu
translations.idiomatic: Yao Tianfu

sentences.zh: 姚天福，字君祥，絳州人。

translations.literal: Yao Tianfu, styled Junxiang, was a man of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Tianfu, styled Junxiang, was a native of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父居實，避兵徙雁門。

translations.literal: His father Jushi, fleeing warfare, moved to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jushi, fleeing warfare, moved to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 天福幼讀《春秋》，通大義。

translations.literal: Tianfu from youth read the Spring and Autumn Annals and understood its great principles.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tianfu read the Spring and Autumn Annals and understood its great principles.

sentences.zh: 及長，以材辟懷仁丞。

translations.literal: When grown, for his talent he was recruited as Assistant of Huairen.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, for his talent he was recruited as Assistant of Huairen.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，詔立御史臺，以天福為閣管勾，尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, an edict established the Censorate; Tianfu was made Pavilion Manager and soon appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhiyuan reign, an edict established the Censorate; Tianfu was made Pavilion Manager and soon appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 每廷折權臣，帝嘉其直，錫名巴兒思，謂其不畏強悍，猶虎也。

translations.literal: Each time in court he refuted powerful ministers; the emperor praised his directness and bestowed the name Barisi, saying he did not fear the strong and fierce—like a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Each time in court he refuted powerful ministers; the emperor praised his directness and bestowed the name Barisi, saying he did not fear the strong and fierce—like a tiger.

sentences.zh: 仍厚賜以旌其忠，天福曰：「臣職居抨彈，惟負爵祿是懼，敢貪厚賞，以重臣罪？

translations.literal: He still richly rewarded him to honor his loyalty. Tianfu said: "Your subject's duty is impeachment; I fear only failing in rank and salary—how dare I greedily accept rich reward and thereby increase my crime as minister?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still richly rewarded him to honor his loyalty. Tianfu said, "Your subject's duty is impeachment; I fear only failing in rank and salary—how dare I greedily accept rich reward and thereby increase my crime as minister?"

sentences.zh: 」時御史臺置二大夫，綱紀無統，天福言於世祖曰：「古稱一蛇九尾，首動尾隨；

translations.literal: " At the time the Censorate had two supervising censors and discipline had no unity. Tianfu said to Kublai: "Antiquity says one snake with nine tails—when the head moves the tails follow;"
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Censorate had two supervising censors and discipline had no unity. Tianfu said to Kublai, "Antiquity says one snake with nine tails—when the head moves the tails follow;"

sentences.zh: 一蛇二首，不能寸進。

translations.literal: one snake with two heads cannot advance an inch.
translations.idiomatic: one snake with two heads cannot advance an inch.

sentences.zh: 今台綱不張，有一蛇二首之患。

translations.literal: Now the censorate's authority is not extended—there is the affliction of one snake with two heads.
translations.idiomatic: Now the censorate's authority is not extended—there is the affliction of one snake with two heads.

sentences.zh: 陛下不急拯之，久則紊不可理。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not urgently rescue it, in time disorder will become impossible to govern.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not urgently rescue it, in time disorder will become impossible to govern.

sentences.zh: 」帝詔玉速帖木兒及孛羅諭之，孛羅以年幼自劾。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered Yisutie'mur and Boluo to be instructed; Boluo impeached himself on grounds of youth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yisutie'mur and Boluo to be instructed; Boluo impeached himself on grounds of youth.

sentences.zh: 天福時按行畿內，有出使者凌民取賄，天福乃易服間行得其狀，奏戮之以徇，豪右懾服。

translations.literal: Tianfu at the time was inspecting within the capital region. There was an outgoing envoy who bullied the people and took bribes. Tianfu changed clothes and traveled secretly to get the facts, memorialized to execute him as a warning, and the powerful were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu at the time was inspecting within the capital region. There was an outgoing envoy who bullied the people and took bribes. Tianfu changed clothes and traveled secretly to get the facts, memorialized to execute him as a warning, and the powerful were awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔罷各道按察司，天福白大夫玉速帖木兒曰：「是司之設，所以廣視聽、虞非常，慮至深遠，不但繩有司而已也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict abolished the Commissions for the Investigation of Crimes in each circuit. Tianfu told Supervising Censor Yisutie'mur: "This office's establishment is to broaden sight and hearing and guard against the unexpected—consideration is deeply far-reaching; it is not merely to bind officials."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, an edict abolished the Commissions for the Investigation of Crimes in each circuit. Tianfu told Supervising Censor Yisutie'mur, "This office's establishment is to broaden sight and hearing and guard against the unexpected—consideration is deeply far-reaching; it is not merely to bind officials."

sentences.zh: 」大夫駭然曰：「微公言，幾失之。

translations.literal: " The supervising censor said in alarm: "But for your words, we would nearly have lost it."
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor said in alarm, "But for your words, we would nearly have lost it."

sentences.zh: 」夜入帝臥內，奏其言，帝大悟，詔復立之。

translations.literal: " That night he entered the emperor's sleeping quarters and memorialized his words; the emperor greatly understood and ordered it re-established.
translations.idiomatic: That night he entered the emperor's sleeping quarters and memorialized his words; the emperor greatly understood and ordered it re-established.

sentences.zh: 權臣不悅，左遷天福朝列大夫、衡州路同知，不就，起為河東道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: Powerful ministers were displeased and demoted Tianfu to Chaolie Doctor and Vice Administrator of Hengzhou Circuit; he did not take office and was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful ministers were displeased and demoted Tianfu to Chaolie Doctor and Vice Administrator of Hengzhou Circuit; he did not take office and was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時北鄙兵興，轉輸煩急，河東民苦徭役。

translations.literal: At the time warfare arose on the northern frontier; transport was urgently burdensome and the people of Hedong suffered from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At the time warfare arose on the northern frontier; transport was urgently burdensome and the people of Hedong suffered from corvée.

sentences.zh: 天福以反側為憂，劾執政失計，奏罷其役。

translations.literal: Tianfu, worried about unrest, impeached the administrators for mistaken planning and memorialized to abolish the corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu, worried about unrest, impeached the administrators for mistaken planning and memorialized to abolish the corvée.

sentences.zh: 徵拜中順大夫、治書侍御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Zhongshun Doctor and Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Zhongshun Doctor and Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，江南既平，授嘉議大夫、淮西道按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, when Jiangnan was pacified, he was granted Jiayi Doctor and Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Huaixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when Jiangnan was pacified, he was granted Jiayi Doctor and Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Huaixi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 淮甸當兵衝，將吏有豪猾為民害者，悉剷除之，民大悅。

translations.literal: The Huai region lay on the military crossroads; among officers and clerks there were fierce and cunning men who harmed the people—all were uprooted and removed; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai region lay on the military crossroads; among officers and clerks there were fierce and cunning men who harmed the people—all were uprooted and removed, and the people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 轉湖北道按察使，發省臣贓事數十以聞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Hubei Circuit and exposed several dozen cases of embezzlement by secretariat officials, reporting them.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Hubei Circuit and exposed several dozen cases of embezzlement by secretariat officials, reporting them to court.

sentences.zh: 帝以其嘗有勳勞，特原之，而流其黨與，州郡稱治。

translations.literal: The emperor, because they had once had merit and labor, specially pardoned them but exiled their associates; prefectures and districts were called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because they had once had merit and labor, specially pardoned them but exiled their associates; prefectures and districts were called well governed.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷山北道按察使，其民鮮知稼穡，天福教以樹藝，皆致蕃富，民為建祠，而刻石以紀之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was transferred to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Shanbei Circuit. Its people rarely knew farming; Tianfu taught them planting and cultivation, and all became prosperous; the people built a shrine for him and carved stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, he was transferred to Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for the Shanbei Circuit. Its people rarely knew farming; Tianfu taught them planting and cultivation, and all became prosperous; the people built a shrine for him and carved stone to record it.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入為刑部尚書，尋出為揚州路總管。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he entered service as Minister of Punishments; soon he went out as Chief Administrator of Yangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, he entered service as Minister of Punishments; soon he went out as Chief Administrator of Yangzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，復為淮西按察使，按巨姦一人，沒其家貲，政化大行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he again became Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for Huaixi; he investigated one great villain, confiscated his family wealth, and good governance was greatly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, he again became Commissioner of the Investigation of Crimes for Huaixi; he investigated one great villain, confiscated his family wealth, and good governance was greatly practiced.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，桑哥敗，考訊黨援，平陽為多，以天福為平陽總管，俾窮治其事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when Sangge fell, party associates were examined; Pingyang had the most. Tianfu was made Chief Administrator of Pingyang and ordered to thoroughly investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, when Sangge fell, party associates were examined; Pingyang had the most. Tianfu was made Chief Administrator of Pingyang and ordered to thoroughly investigate the matter.

sentences.zh: 俄拜甘肅行省參知政事，以母老辭。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Gansu Branch Secretariat but declined on grounds of his mother's age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Gansu Branch Secretariat but declined on grounds of his mother's age.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，授陝西漢中道肅政廉訪使，尋除真定路總管。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, he was granted Commissioner for Rectifying Governance and Investigating Corruption of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit; soon he was appointed Chief Administrator of Zhending Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, he was granted Commissioner for Rectifying Governance and Investigating Corruption of the Shaanxi Hanzhong Circuit; soon he was appointed Chief Administrator of Zhending Circuit.

sentences.zh: 真定驛傳之需，多為民害，天福更議措置之方，使不擾民，憲長爭之。

translations.literal: The needs of Zhending's courier stations mostly harmed the people. Tianfu reconsidered methods of arrangement so as not to disturb the people; the censorial chief disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: The needs of Zhending's courier stations mostly harmed the people. Tianfu reconsidered methods of arrangement so as not to disturb the people; the censorial chief disputed it.

sentences.zh: 省臣以其事聞，詔從之，頒其制為天下式。

translations.literal: Branch secretariat officials reported the matter; an edict followed it and promulgated its system as the model for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Branch secretariat officials reported the matter; an edict followed it and promulgated its system as the model for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，授江西行省參政，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, he was granted Vice Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat but declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dade reign, he was granted Vice Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat but declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜參知政事、大都路總管、兼大興府尹，畿甸大治。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Vice Director, Chief Administrator of Dadu Circuit, and concurrently Prefect of Daxing Prefecture; the capital region was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was appointed Vice Director, Chief Administrator of Dadu Circuit, and concurrently Prefect of Daxing Prefecture; the capital region was greatly well governed.

sentences.zh: 後之尹京者，以天福為稱首。

translations.literal: Later prefects of the capital took Tianfu as foremost in reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Later prefects of the capital took Tianfu as foremost in reputation.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he died of illness, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he died of illness, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 初，天福拜御史時，其母戒之曰：「古稱公爾忘私，委質為臣，當罄所衷，以塞其職，勿以未亡人為卹，俾吾追踪陵母，死之日猶生之年也。

translations.literal: Initially, when Tianfu was appointed censor, his mother admonished him: "Antiquity says public duty makes one forget private interest. Having entrusted oneself as minister, one should exhaust one's innermost heart to fulfill the duty—do not take the not-yet-deceased person as cause for concern, so that I may follow the mother of Ling: the day of death would still be the year of life."
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Tianfu was appointed censor, his mother admonished him, "Antiquity says public duty makes one forget private interest. Having entrusted oneself as minister, one should exhaust one's innermost heart to fulfill the duty—do not take me, your not-yet-deceased mother, as cause for concern, so that I may follow the mother of Ling: the day of death would still be the year of life."

sentences.zh: 」天福亦請於憲府曰：「監察責當言路，有犯無隱，苟獲譴，乞不為親累。

translations.literal: " Tianfu also requested of the censorate: "Supervising censors are responsible for the path of speech—if there is offense, do not hide it. If punishment is received, I beg that my kin not be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu also requested of the censorate, "Supervising censors are responsible for the path of speech—if there is offense, do not hide it. If punishment is received, I beg that my kin not be implicated."

sentences.zh: 」或以聞，帝歎曰：「巴兒思母子雖生今世，其義烈之言當於古人中求之。」

translations.literal: " This was reported; the emperor sighed and said: "Barisi and his mother, though living in the present age, their words of righteous valor should be sought among the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: This was reported; the emperor sighed and said, "Barisi and his mother, though living in the present age, their words of righteous valor should be sought among the ancients."

sentences.zh: 子祖舜，秘書監著作郎；

translations.literal: His son Zushun was Compiler of the Secretariat Directorate;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zushun served as Compiler of the Secretariat Directorate;

sentences.zh: 侃，內藏庫副使。

translations.literal: Kan was Vice Commissioner of the Inner Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Kan served as Vice Commissioner of the Inner Treasury.

sentences.zh: ○許國禎

translations.literal: ○ Xu Guozhen
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guozhen

sentences.zh: 許國禎，字進之，絳州曲沃人也。

translations.literal: Xu Guozhen, styled Jinzhi, was a man of Quwo in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guozhen, styled Jinzhi, was a native of Quwo in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖濟，金絳州節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji was Military Commissioner of Jiang Prefecture under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji was Military Commissioner of Jiang Prefecture under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父日嚴，榮州節度判官。

translations.literal: His father Riyan was Adjutant Military Commissioner of Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Riyan was Adjutant Military Commissioner of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 皆業醫。

translations.literal: All practiced medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The family practiced medicine for generations.

sentences.zh: 國禎博通經史，尤精醫術。

translations.literal: Guozhen broadly mastered the classics and histories and was especially skilled in medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen broadly mastered the classics and histories and was especially skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 金亂，避地嵩州永寧縣。

translations.literal: When Jin was in turmoil, he fled to Yongning County in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin was in turmoil, he fled to Yongning County in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河南平，歸寓太原。

translations.literal: When Henan was pacified, he returned and settled in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan was pacified, he returned and settled in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸，國禎以醫徵至翰海，留守掌醫藥。

translations.literal: When Kublai was in the princely establishment, Guozhen was summoned as physician to Hanhai and remained to manage medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai was in the princely establishment, Guozhen was summoned as physician to Hanhai and remained to manage medicine.

sentences.zh: 莊聖太后有疾，國禎治之，刻期而愈，乃張晏賜坐。

translations.literal: Empress Zhuang Sheng was ill; Guozhen treated her and she recovered on schedule. Thereupon a banquet was spread and he was granted a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhuang Sheng was ill; Guozhen treated her and she recovered on schedule. Thereupon a banquet was spread and he was granted a seat.

sentences.zh: 太后時年五十三，遂以白金鋌如年數賜之。

translations.literal: The empress was then fifty-three; she therefore bestowed white gold ingots equal to her years.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was then fifty-three; she therefore bestowed white gold ingots equal to her years.

sentences.zh: 伯撒王妃病目，治者針誤損其明。

translations.literal: Princess Consort Bosa had an eye ailment; the treater's needle mistakenly damaged her sight.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Consort Bosa had an eye ailment; the treater's needle mistakenly damaged her sight.

sentences.zh: 世祖怒，欲坐以死罪，國禎從容諫曰：「罪固當死，然原其情乃恐怖失次所致。

translations.literal: Kublai was angry and wished to punish with death. Guozhen calmly remonstrated: "The crime indeed deserves death, yet tracing the circumstances, it arose from terror and loss of composure."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was angry and wished to punish with death. Guozhen calmly remonstrated, "The crime indeed deserves death, yet tracing the circumstances, it arose from terror and loss of composure."

sentences.zh: 即誅之，後誰敢復進？

translations.literal: If he is executed now, who afterward will dare to advance?
translations.idiomatic: If he is executed now, who afterward will dare to advance?

sentences.zh: 」世祖意解，且獎之曰：「國禎之直，可作諫官。

translations.literal: " Kublai's mind was eased, and he also praised him: "Guozhen's directness could serve as remonstrating official."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai's mind was eased, and he also praised him, "Guozhen's directness could serve as remonstrating official."

sentences.zh: 」宗王昔班屢請以國禎隸帳下，世祖重違其請，將遣之，辭曰：「國禎蒙恩拔擢，誓盡心以報，不敢易所事。

translations.literal: " Prince Xiban repeatedly requested that Guozhen be subordinated to his establishment. Kublai greatly wished not to refuse his request and was about to dispatch him. Guozhen declined: "Guozhen has received grace and elevation; I swear to exhaust my heart in repayment and dare not change whom I serve."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiban repeatedly requested that Guozhen be subordinated to his establishment. Kublai greatly wished not to refuse his request and was about to dispatch him. Guozhen declined, "Guozhen has received grace and elevation; I swear to exhaust my heart in repayment and dare not change whom I serve."

sentences.zh: 」乃不果遣。

translations.literal: " He was then not dispatched after all.
translations.idiomatic: He was then not dispatched after all.

sentences.zh: 世祖過飲馬湩，得足疾，國禎進藥味苦，卻不服，國禎曰：「古人有言：良藥苦口利於病，忠言逆耳利於行。

translations.literal: Kublai drank too much kumiss and got a foot ailment. Guozhen presented medicine that tasted bitter; he refused to take it. Guozhen said: "The ancients have a saying: good medicine is bitter in the mouth but benefits the illness; loyal words are harsh to the ear but benefit conduct."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai drank too much kumiss and got a foot ailment. Guozhen presented medicine that tasted bitter; he refused to take it. Guozhen said, "The ancients have a saying: good medicine is bitter in the mouth but benefits the illness; loyal words are harsh to the ear but benefit conduct."

sentences.zh: 」已而足疾再作，召國禎入視，世祖曰：「不聽汝言，果困斯疾。

translations.literal: " Before long the foot ailment recurred; Guozhen was summoned to examine him. Kublai said: "Not listening to your words, I was indeed afflicted by this illness."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the foot ailment recurred; Guozhen was summoned to examine him. Kublai said, "Not listening to your words, I was indeed afflicted by this illness."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「良藥苦口既知之矣，忠言逆耳願留意焉。

translations.literal: " He replied: "You already know that good medicine is bitter in the mouth; please also heed that loyal words are harsh to the ear."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "You already know that good medicine is bitter in the mouth; please also heed that loyal words are harsh to the ear."

sentences.zh: 」世祖大悅，以七寶馬鞍賜之。

translations.literal: " Kublai was greatly pleased and bestowed on him a saddle of seven treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was greatly pleased and bestowed on him a saddle of seven treasures.

sentences.zh: 憲宗三年癸丑，從征雲南，機密皆得參與，朝夕未嘗離左右。

translations.literal: In the third year of Möngke, year guichou, he followed the campaign against Yunnan; confidential matters he all participated in; morning and evening he never left Kublai's side.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Möngke, year guichou, he followed the campaign against Yunnan; confidential matters he all participated in; morning and evening he never left Kublai's side.

sentences.zh: 或在告，帝輒為之不悅。

translations.literal: When he was on leave, the emperor was displeased on his account.
translations.idiomatic: When he was on leave, the emperor was displeased on his account.

sentences.zh: 九年己未，世祖帥師圍鄂州，獲宋人數百族，諸將欲盡坑之，國禎力請止誅其凶暴，餘皆獲免。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, year jiwei, Kublai led troops to besiege E Prefecture and captured several hundred Song clans. The generals wished to bury them all alive; Guozhen forcefully pleaded to stop, executing only the violent and cruel—the rest were all spared.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, year jiwei, Kublai led troops to besiege E Prefecture and captured several hundred Song clans. The generals wished to bury them all alive; Guozhen forcefully pleaded to stop, executing only the violent and cruel—the rest were all spared.

sentences.zh: 及師還，招降民數十萬口，疲餓顛仆者滿道，國禎白髮蔡州軍儲糧賑之，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: When the army returned, surrendered people numbered hundreds of thousands; the exhausted, hungry, and fallen filled the roads. Guozhen reported and dispatched Cai Prefecture military stores grain to relieve them; very many were preserved alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, surrendered people numbered hundreds of thousands; the exhausted, hungry, and fallen filled the roads. Guozhen reported and dispatched Cai Prefecture military stores grain to relieve them; very many were preserved alive.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，錄前勞，授榮祿大夫、提點太醫院事，賜金符。

translations.literal: When Kublai ascended the throne, he recorded former labor and appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Academy, bestowing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai ascended the throne, he recorded former labor and appointed him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Academy, bestowing a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，改授金虎符。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, he was changed to a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhiyuan reign, he was changed to a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, he was transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 國禎嘗上疏言：慎財賦、禁服色、明法律、嚴武備、設諫官、均衛兵、建學校、立朝儀，事多施行。

translations.literal: Guozhen once memorialized: be careful with finances and levies, forbid improper dress and colors, clarify laws, strengthen military preparedness, establish remonstrating officials, equalize guard troops, build schools, establish court ceremony—many matters were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen once memorialized: be careful with finances and levies, forbid improper dress and colors, clarify laws, strengthen military preparedness, establish remonstrating officials, equalize guard troops, build schools, establish court ceremony—many matters were implemented.

sentences.zh: 凡所薦引，皆知名士，士亦歸重之。

translations.literal: All those he recommended were famous scholars; scholars also looked to him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: All those he recommended were famous scholars; scholars also looked to him with respect.

sentences.zh: 帝與近臣言及勳舊大臣，因謂國禎曰：「朕昔出征，同履艱難者，惟卿數人在爾。

translations.literal: The emperor, speaking with close ministers of meritorious old great ministers, then said to Guozhen: "When I formerly went on campaign, those who shared hardship with me are only you few."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, speaking with close ministers of meritorious old great ministers, then said to Guozhen, "When I formerly went on campaign, those who shared hardship with me are only you few."

sentences.zh: 」遂拜集賢大學士，進階光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies and advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies and advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 每進見，帝呼為許光祿而不名，由是內外諸王大臣皆以許光祿呼之。

translations.literal: Each time he had audience, the emperor called him Grand Master Xu without using his name; from this inner and outer princes and great ministers all called him Grand Master Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he had audience, the emperor called him Grand Master Xu without using his name; from this inner and outer princes and great ministers all called him Grand Master Xu.

sentences.zh: 升翰林集賢大學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Academician of the Hanlin and Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Academician of the Hanlin and Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十六。

translations.literal: He died aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 時大臣非有勳德為帝所知者，罕得贈諡，特贈國禎金紫光祿大夫，諡忠憲，人以為榮。

translations.literal: At the time great ministers who lacked merit and virtue known to the emperor rarely received posthumous ennoblement and posthumous names; Guozhen was specially posthumously granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with the posthumous name Zhongxian—people considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time great ministers who lacked merit and virtue known to the emperor rarely received posthumous ennoblement and posthumous names; Guozhen was specially posthumously granted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon with the posthumous name Zhongxian—people considered it an honor.

sentences.zh: 後加贈推誠廣德協恭翊亮功臣、翰林學士承旨、上柱國，追封薊國公。

translations.literal: Later he was further posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Sincerity, Broad Virtue, Harmonious Respect, and Assisting Brightness, Academician Expositor of the Hanlin Academy, and Senior Pillar of the State, ennobled as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Sincerity, Broad Virtue, Harmonious Respect, and Assisting Brightness, Academician Expositor of the Hanlin Academy, and Senior Pillar of the State, ennobled as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 初，國禎母韓氏，亦以能醫侍莊聖太后，又善調和食味，稱旨，凡四方所獻珍膳旨酒，皆命掌之。

translations.literal: Initially, Guozhen's mother Lady Han, also skilled in medicine, attended Empress Zhuang Sheng; she was also good at harmonizing food flavors and accorded with the imperial intent. All rare delicacies and fine wines presented from the four directions were ordered managed by her.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Guozhen's mother Lady Han, also skilled in medicine, attended Empress Zhuang Sheng; she was also good at harmonizing food flavors and accorded with the imperial intent. All rare delicacies and fine wines presented from the four directions were ordered managed by her.

sentences.zh: 太后閔其勞，賜以真定宅一區，歲給衣廩終身，國禎由是家焉。

translations.literal: The empress pitied her labor and bestowed one residence in Zhending, supplying clothing and grain annually for life; Guozhen thereby made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: The empress pitied her labor and bestowed one residence in Zhending, supplying clothing and grain annually for life; Guozhen thereby made his home there.

sentences.zh: 子扆。

translations.literal: His son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi.

sentences.zh: 扆字君黼，一名忽魯火孫，從其父國禎事世祖於潛邸，進退莊重，世祖喜之，賜今名。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Junfu, one name Huluhuosun, followed his father Guozhen in serving Kublai at the princely establishment. In comings and goings he was dignified and solemn; Kublai was pleased and bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Junfu, also known as Huluhuosun, followed his father Guozhen in serving Kublai at the princely establishment. In comings and goings he was dignified and solemn, and Kublai was pleased and bestowed his present name.

sentences.zh: 俾從許衡學，入備宿衛，忠慎小心。

translations.literal: He was made to study with Xu Heng, entered palace guard service, and was loyal, cautious, and careful.
translations.idiomatic: He was made to study with Xu Heng, entered palace guard service, and was loyal, cautious, and careful.

sentences.zh: 嘗因事忤旨，欲罪之，帝后悔，謂近侍帖哥曰：「朕欲罪忽魯火孫，汝何不言？

translations.literal: Once because of a matter he opposed the imperial intent and was to be punished. The emperor later regretted it and said to close attendant Tiege: "I wished to punish Huluhuosun—why did you not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Once because of a matter he opposed the imperial intent and was to be punished. The emperor later regretted it and said to close attendant Tiege, "I wished to punish Huluhuosun—why did you not speak?"

sentences.zh: 汝二人自今結為兄弟，有所譴責，則更相進諫。

translations.literal: You two from now on shall be bound as brothers; when there is reproach or punishment, you shall remonstrate with one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: You two from now on shall be bound as brothers; when there is reproach or punishment, you shall remonstrate with one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 」乃置金酒中，賜二人飲，以為盟。

translations.literal: " He then placed gold in wine and bestowed it for the two to drink, making it a covenant.
translations.idiomatic: He then placed gold in wine and bestowed it for the two to drink, making it a covenant.

sentences.zh: 時裕宗居東宮，帝又諭忽魯火孫曰：「若太子罪汝，將誰諫耶？

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Zong lived in the Eastern Palace. The emperor again instructed Huluhuosun: "If the crown prince punishes you, who will remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Crown Prince Zong lived in the Eastern Palace. The emperor again instructed Huluhuosun, "If the crown prince punishes you, who will remonstrate?"

sentences.zh: 」遂命東宮臣慶山奴亦同飲金酒。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Eastern Palace minister Qingshannu also to drink the gold wine together.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Eastern Palace minister Qingshannu also to drink the gold wine together.

sentences.zh: 俄除禮部尚書、提點太醫院事，賜日月龍鳳紋綺衣二襲。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Rites and Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Academy and bestowed two suits of brocade robes patterned with sun, moon, dragon, and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Minister of Rites and Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Academy and bestowed two suits of brocade robes patterned with sun, moon, dragon, and phoenix.

sentences.zh: 每外國使至，必命與之語，辭理明辨，莫不傾服。

translations.literal: Whenever foreign envoys arrived, he was always ordered to converse with them. His reasoning was clear and discerning; none failed to be won over.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever foreign envoys arrived, he was always ordered to converse with them. His reasoning was clear and discerning, and none failed to be won over.

sentences.zh: 改尚醫太監。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director of the Imperial Physicians.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Director of the Imperial Physicians.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗命畫工寫其像賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered painters to render his portrait and bestow it on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered painters to render his portrait and bestow it on him.

sentences.zh: 轉正議大夫，仍提點太醫院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhengyi Doctor and still served as Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zhengyi Doctor while continuing as Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Academy.

sentences.zh: 有竊大安閣禮神之幣者，將誅之，群臣莫敢言，忽魯火孫獨諫曰：「敬神，善事也。

translations.literal: Someone stole the ritual silks for honoring spirits at the Da'an Pavilion and was to be executed. None of the ministers dared speak; Huluhuosun alone remonstrated: "Revering the spirits is a good deed."
translations.idiomatic: Someone stole the ritual silks for honoring spirits at the Da'an Pavilion and was to be executed. None of the ministers dared speak; Huluhuosun alone remonstrated, "Revering the spirits is a good deed."

sentences.zh: 因置人於死地，臣恐神不享所祭。

translations.literal: Yet because of it to put a man to death—I fear the spirits will not accept the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of it to put a man to death—I fear the spirits will not accept the offering.

sentences.zh: 」帝即命釋之。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately ordered him released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 忽魯火孫與丞相安童善，國政多所贊益，桑哥忌之，數譖於上，帝不之信。

translations.literal: Huluhuosun was on good terms with Chief Counselor An Tong and contributed much to state affairs. Sangge envied him and repeatedly slandered him to the throne; the emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Huluhuosun was on good terms with Chief Counselor An Tong and contributed much to state affairs. Sangge envied him and repeatedly slandered him to the throne, but the emperor did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 桑哥敗，係於左掖門，帝命忽魯火孫往唾其面，辭不可，帝稱其仁厚，賜以白玉帶。

translations.literal: When Sangge fell, he was bound at the Left Flank Gate. The emperor ordered Huluhuosun to go spit in his face; he declined as improper. The emperor praised his benevolence and generosity and bestowed a white jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangge fell, he was bound at the Left Flank Gate. The emperor ordered Huluhuosun to go spit in his face; he declined as improper. The emperor praised his benevolence and generosity and bestowed a white jade belt.

sentences.zh: 且諭之曰：「以汝明潔無瑕，有類此玉，故以賜汝也。

translations.literal: Moreover he instructed him: "Because you are bright, pure, and without flaw, like this jade, therefore it is bestowed on you."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he instructed him, "Because you are bright, pure, and without flaw, like this jade, therefore it is bestowed on you."

sentences.zh: 」成宗即位，遷中書右丞，行太常卿。

translations.literal: " When Chengzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Right Director of the Secretariat and Acting Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Right Director of the Secretariat and Acting Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 力辭，乃命以中書右丞署太常事。

translations.literal: He forcefully declined; he was then ordered as Right Director of the Secretariat to manage ceremonial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully declined and was then ordered as Right Director of the Secretariat to manage ceremonial affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄改陝西行中書省右丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Right Director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reassigned as Right Director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時關中飢，議發倉粟賑之，同列以未得請於朝不可，忽魯火孫曰：「民為邦本，今飢餒如此，若俟命下，無及矣。

translations.literal: At the time Guanzhong was in famine; they discussed issuing granary grain to relieve it. Colleagues said permission from court had not been obtained and it could not be done. Huluhuosun said: "The people are the foundation of the state. Now hunger and starvation are such—if we wait for orders to come down, it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Guanzhong was in famine and they discussed issuing granary grain to relieve it. Colleagues said permission from court had not been obtained and it could not be done. Huluhuosun said, "The people are the foundation of the state. Hunger and starvation are such now that if we wait for orders to come down, it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 擅發之罪，吾當獨任之，不以累公等。

translations.literal: The crime of unauthorized issuance—I shall bear it alone and not implicate you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The crime of unauthorized issuance I shall bear alone and not implicate you gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 」遂大發粟，不數日命亦下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon grain was greatly issued; within a few days the order also came down.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon grain was greatly issued; within a few days the order also came down.

sentences.zh: 明年旱，禱於終南山而雨，歲以大熟，民皆畫像祀之。

translations.literal: The next year there was drought; he prayed at Mount Zhongnan and rain fell; the year had great harvest, and the people all painted portraits to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year there was drought; he prayed at Mount Zhongnan and rain fell. The year had a great harvest, and the people all painted portraits to honor him.

sentences.zh: 忽魯火孫不事生業，田宅皆上所賜。

translations.literal: Huluhuosun did not engage in livelihood pursuits; fields and residences were all bestowed by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Huluhuosun did not engage in livelihood pursuits; his fields and residences were all bestowed by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 有足疾，不能行，仁宗以為先朝老臣，特敕乘小輿入禁中，訪以舊事。

translations.literal: He had a foot ailment and could not walk. Renzong, considering him an old minister of the former court, specially ordered him to ride a small palanquin into the forbidden precincts and consulted him on old affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had a foot ailment and could not walk. Renzong, considering him an old minister of the former court, specially ordered him to ride a small palanquin into the forbidden precincts and consulted him on old affairs.

sentences.zh: 後足益弱，不可出，每國有大政，詔使近侍即其家問之。

translations.literal: Later his feet grew weaker and he could not go out. Whenever the state had great policies, an edict sent close attendants to his home to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Later his feet grew weaker and he could not go out. Whenever the state had great policies, an edict sent close attendants to his home to inquire.

sentences.zh: 特授榮祿大夫、大司徒，食其祿終身。

translations.literal: He was specially granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Minister of Education and received salary for life.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Minister of Education and received salary for life.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠守正佐理功臣、光祿大夫、陝西

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Rectitude, and Assisted Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Shaanxi
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Rectitude, and Assisted Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Shaanxi

sentences.zh: 等處行中書省平章政事、柱國，追封趙國公，諡僖簡。

translations.literal: and other places Branch Secretariat Vice Director, Pillar of the State, ennobled as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous name Xijian.
translations.idiomatic: and other places Branch Secretariat Vice Director, Pillar of the State, ennobled as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous name Xijian.
